# oxc-react-docgen

React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax.

> **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete.

## Why

`react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system that takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish.

OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass:

- **Cold extraction, 21 real component libraries:** 50ms ([full breakdown](docs/benchmarks.md))
- **Incremental single-file update:** ~2ms — react-docgen-typescript has no equivalent API; every edit re-pays the full cold cost

The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet.

## Install

> Not yet on npm. No prebuilt per-platform binaries exist yet — build from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper
cd caliper
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi run build:napi   # builds the native addon for your platform
pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin build
```

Use `pnpm run build:napi`, not a bare `cargo build` — it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s loader expects it.

Migrating off `react-docgen-typescript`? See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) for what's compatible today.

## Vite plugin

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { oxcReactDocgen } from '@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin'

14	
15	- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
16	- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.

name: Release & Publish

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged Callisto release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

# Registry credentials exist only inside `execute`.
permissions: {}

# Per-commit group: a shared group would drop a queued release merge.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Keep in lockstep with .prototools.
  RUST_VERSION: "1.98.1"

jobs:
  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Scheduling hint only; `callisto release plan` is the authority.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 15
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # Pinned here, not inherited from the action's default.
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.8.0
          verification: require
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # Core bumps otherwise leave path-dependents stale in Cargo.lock.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Derive release intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.8.0
          verification: require
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --profile production \
            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          shasum -a 256 "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json" > "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json.sha256"
      # No `[release]` section here, so callisto-managed artifact slots are unexpected.
      - name: Reject unexpected artifact slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$(jq '.artifactSlots | length' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")" != "0" ]]; then
            echo "::error::intent declares artifact slots but this workflow has no build job"
            exit 1
          fi
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # Long enough to re-run `execute` after a multi-day diagnosis.
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.platform }}
    needs: [release-candidate, plan]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.host }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        include:
          - { host: macos-latest, target: aarch64-apple-darwin, platform: darwin-arm64, bin: oxc-react-docgen }
          - { host: macos-latest, target: x86_64-apple-darwin, platform: darwin-x64, bin: oxc-react-docgen }
          - { host: ubuntu-latest, target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, platform: linux-x64-gnu, bin: oxc-react-docgen }
          - { host: ubuntu-latest, target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, platform: linux-arm64-gnu, bin: oxc-react-docgen, zig: true }
          - { host: windows-latest, target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, platform: win32-x64-msvc, bin: oxc-react-docgen.exe }
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      # No caches in release builds.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
          cache: false
      - run: |
          rustup toolchain install "$RUST_VERSION" --profile minimal --target "$TARGET" --no-self-update
          rustup default "$RUST_VERSION"
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
      - if: matrix.zig
        uses: mlugg/setup-zig@d1434d08867e3ee9daa34448df10607b98908d29 # v2.2.1
        with:
          version: 0.14.1
          use-cache: false
      - if: matrix.zig
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: cargo-zigbuild
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi
      - name: Build napi addon
        working-directory: packages/napi
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          ZIG: ${{ matrix.zig }}
        run: pnpm napi build --platform --release --target "$TARGET" ${ZIG:+--cross-compile} --manifest-path ../../crates/binding/Cargo.toml --output-dir .
      - name: Build CLI binary
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          ZIG: ${{ matrix.zig }}
        run: cargo "${ZIG:+zig}build" --release --locked -p oxc-react-docgen --target "$TARGET"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: napi-${{ matrix.platform }}
          path: packages/napi/oxc_react_docgen_napi.${{ matrix.platform }}.node
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: cli-${{ matrix.platform }}
          path: target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/${{ matrix.bin }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [release-candidate, plan, build]
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Merging the release PR is the approval; no environment gate.
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    env:
      NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # Needs callisto >= 0.9.0 (gitignored release-source files, platform-package publish).
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.8.0
          verification: require
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Tag dispatch pushes from here.
          persist-credentials: true
      # Outside release-source: callisto rejects non-ignored untracked files there.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: napi-*
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-artifacts
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: cli-*
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/cli-artifacts
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
          cache: false
      - name: Install deps and place platform binaries
        working-directory: release-source
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          (cd packages/napi && pnpm napi artifacts --output-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/napi-artifacts")
          for dir in "${RUNNER_TEMP}"/cli-artifacts/cli-*; do
            platform="${dir##*/cli-}"
            dest="packages/cli/npm/${platform}"
            [[ -d "$dest" ]] || { echo "::error::no package dir for $platform"; exit 1; }
            mv "$dir"/* "$dest/"
            chmod +x "$dest"/oxc-react-docgen*
          done
          for dir in packages/napi/npm/* packages/cli/npm/*; do
            files=$(jq -r '.files[]' "$dir/package.json")
            for f in $files; do
              [[ -f "$dir/$f" ]] || { echo "::error::missing $dir/$f"; exit 1; }
            done
          done
      # npm and pnpm both read the user-level .npmrc.
      - name: Authenticate with the npm registry
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken "$NPM_TOKEN"
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          receipt_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$receipt_dir"
          args=(
            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source"
            --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json"
            --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json"
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
            --profile production
          )
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Upload receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-receipt
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-receipt/${{ github.run_id }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

# Releasing

How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.

For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).

---

## Local release: `callisto release`

`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.

- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` can print `Nothing to release.` without a receipt.

- That message is not proof of completion.
- Generated simple workflows share this limit.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build/placement roster is currently workspace-wide, not narrowed to the release intent. Unrelated addons can block a release; this is tracked for correction, not a support requirement.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning and build jobs, and action inputs.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and an explicit full release-source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code, create a version PR, or invent a newer version.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs". Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes, the npm dist-tag, or a complete Python wheel/sdist set. A partial PyPI upload can therefore be mistaken for a complete version. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

---

## Platform-package publish order

`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.

A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.

- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.

For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.
=== 0.9.0
- callisto release --dry-run and callisto release plan now include a diagnostics array in their JSON output when an artifact owner package is selected without its product package, instead of only printing a stderr warning.
- callisto version now refreshes npm, pnpm, yarn, bun and pdm lockfiles by default (in addition to Cargo, uv and poetry), opt out with --no-refresh-lockfiles; a failed refresh now stops the command with a coded error naming the lockfile and command
- A dependent released in the same run has its spec on a bumped internal dependency raised to the new version, even when the old spec still covers it.
- Generated release workflows pass the detected default branch to the release-PR action, and `init` now resolves it from a live remote query or the checked-out branch when `origin/HEAD` isn't set locally, instead of silently defaulting to `main`.
- **Git runs through the system `git` binary only**
  
  The in-process gitoxide backend is gone; every Git read and write already had to work through the `git` binary the CLI requires. Commit inference keeps a commit that touched a package even when a later merge discarded its change (`git log --full-history`), matching the removed backend. An annotated release tag made with no Git identity configured takes the target commit's committer as its tagger.
  
  Breaking:
  - `callisto_model::vcs` (was `callisto-vcs`): removed `GitRepository`, `ShellGit`, the `GitDataSource` trait and the revwalk visit counter. `GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` is now `GitAccess::new(root, runner)` with inherent methods.
  - `callisto_model::vcs`: `commits_since` with an unresolvable `since` ref returns `VcsError::RefNotFound` (was `VcsError::Git` from the shell path).
- Shell completions no longer offer hidden plumbing subcommands, at any nesting depth
- snapshot rewrites every dependency spec the snapshot version falls outside of, so cargo metadata resolves after a snapshot
- Loading a workspace now fails with a clear error naming both directories when two of them declare the same ecosystem and name, instead of silently routing dependency edges to the wrong package.
- Fixed groups compute their shared version from the highest member version when no member is tagged, support PEP 440 versions, and follow pre-release mode. Before, an untagged group could be bumped down to 0.x.
- `callisto init` can generate `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (the workflow path release artifact attestations are bound to) for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages and no shipped release artifacts: interactive question or `--workflow`/`--no-workflow` (mutually exclusive), refuses to overwrite an existing file (checked before the preview, including under `--dry-run`). After writing the file, init prints that a merge to the default branch publishes, so that branch should require pull requests and reviews. JSON output carries the same text as a `workflow-merge-publishes` diagnostic with the new `info` severity. The generated file is two jobs (`version-pr`, `release`) under 40 lines, triggered on push to the detected default branch, with per-job permissions and secrets wired per detected ecosystem (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_TOKEN`; npm workspaces also set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` so publishes carry provenance), pinned to `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<commit>` -- resolved from the `callisto@<version>` release tag, since a GitHub Actions `uses:` ref is split at the *last* `@` in the string, so the tag can't be written into `uses:` directly.
  
  `callisto-action` gains a `mode: version-pr | release` input (default `version-pr`, unchanged behavior); `mode: release` installs Callisto and runs `callisto release`, filling `published`/`publishedPackages` from its receipt. An invalid mode fails naming the accepted values. Its environment-setup step no longer references sibling action `setup-callisto` through `uses:` (`$/` and an external `owner/repo/path@ref` both resolve against whichever ref invoked the *top-level* workflow, not necessarily this action's own) -- it now calls `setup-callisto`'s install script directly by `github.action_path`, so it always uses its own checked-out ref, including when invoked from another repository's workflow.
- Workspace discovery no longer silently drops or misattaches packages: a manifest that fails to parse now fails with a clear error naming the path when it's a real workspace member, and warns otherwise; root detection asks git itself instead of hand-walking for .git, so GIT_DIR and worktrees are respected, and it reads [workspace]/[package] as real TOML tables instead of matching the text (a commented-out mention no longer counts); a platform package sitting beside its own Cargo.toml or pyproject.toml is never misattached to an unrelated owner; and a [[package]] rule that matches no packages gets a warning, matching the existing [[package-set]] one.
- Every add/version/schema/pre/release-pr error now carries its own code and help text instead of a generic message; release-pr decide/verify report the exact invalid-branch or duplicate-pull-request code instead of a plain string when reading a snapshot or decision from a file, inline JSON, or stdin.
- callisto init and callisto release --dry-run in a repository without an origin remote no longer print a stray git error about the missing remote.
- **`callisto init` asks for intent and previews the first release**
  
  `init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resulting `callisto.toml` and the first release plan from the same derivation as `release --dry-run`, then writes after confirmation. Non-default tag conventions (`{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}`, `v{version}`) are detected and kept. Non-interactive: `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`, plus `--artifact-target`, `--forge-repository`, `--product-package` to ship binaries. In a repository with no commit yet, `init` writes the config and skips the preview.
  
  Root discovery stays inside the Git repository: the nearest workspace manifest wins, otherwise the outermost package manifest (`Cargo.toml` with `[package]`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml`), so a single-package repository works for every command and `vendor/` or `node_modules/` packages never shadow it.
  
  Breaking:
  - `init` refuses an existing `callisto.toml`; the `[init]` reconcile flow is gone (an `[init]` table still loads and is ignored).
  - A non-terminal run needs `--yes --versioning`; `init --yes` alone errors.
  - `init` requires a Git repository with an `origin` remote.
  - Every command errors outside a Git repository (E058) and never searches above its root.
  - A forge repository other than `origin`'s GitHub repository is refused.
  - The written config holds only answers: no `[changesets]`, `[cascade]`, or `[init]` defaults.
  - `InitReport` JSON drops `diff` and adds `config`.
- Fix: a changeset with any unresolved package entry is no longer consumed, so its bump is not silently lost
- Text output now names registries (crates.io, npm, PyPI) and diagnostic severities in plain, lowercase words instead of internal identifiers
- Skip a private, versionless root package.json (standard npm/pnpm monorepo layout) instead of failing status/version with a missing-version error.
- callisto help <command> now prints that command's help text, including nested subcommands like callisto help pre enter
- init warns about each .changeset/config.json key it does not honour
- init rejects --forge-repository and --product-package up front when --artifact-target isn't given, instead of silently ignoring them
- An empty changeset (the shape `@changesets/cli add --empty` writes) is now accepted instead of rejected; status reports an entries-empty changeset as advisory instead of an error, and reports each unparseable changeset as a per-file error instead of aborting the whole command
- Install callisto with proto: `proto/callisto.toml` downloads the release binary for macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 (glibc or musl). moon tasks run the installed CLI.
  
  Breaking:
  - Removed the moon extension (`callisto-moon` crate) and the `callisto-moon.wasm` release asset. Use the proto plugin and run `callisto` from moon tasks.
  - Removed the moon project-graph cross-check: `ProjectLocator::declared_edges`, `DeclaredEdge`, `DeclaredEdgeKind`, `DiagnosticCode::GraphEdgeDisagreement` and `LocateError::{MoonUnavailable, MoonOutputParse, IncompatibleMoonVersion}`. With it go `--strict-graph` on `status`, `version` and `snapshot`, `StrictFlag::StrictGraph`, and the `strict_graph` fields of `StatusOptions`/`VersionOptions`; `escalate` takes only `strict`.
  - Removed `IdentityResolver` and its errors `GraphError::UnsupportedIdentityEcosystem` (E155) and `GraphError::PackageIdentifierParse` (E156); the `callisto-cli` `wrapper` feature is gone.
- **Generated release workflows build split napi layouts**
  
  `callisto matrix` adds `manifestPath` to a napi target whose addon crate is outside the npm package's directory (e.g. `packages/napi` with the crate in `crates/binding`): the workspace `cdylib` depending on `napi` whose lib name equals `napi.binaryName`. The generated workflow passes it to `napi build --manifest-path`. No single match fails with E204, listing the candidates.
  
  The generated workflow also runs `npx --package @napi-rs/cli@3.10.4 napi ...`: the bare `npx @napi-rs/cli@3.10.4` form fails because the package has two bins.
- init's report now lists every file it wrote (or, under --dry-run, would write), including the generated workflow and .changeset/README.md
- **npm platform packages release with their owner**
  
  An `os`/`cpu` package listed in another package's `optionalDependencies` is now part of that owner: same version, no tag, pins kept in sync, published with `npm publish <dir>` before the owner. Covers napi addons and esbuild-style CLIs, including `npm/<platform>` dirs outside workspace globs. No `[[fixed-group]]` entry needed.
  
  Breaking:
  - Release intents are schema v4; re-plan intents made by older versions.
=== 0.10.0
- Output that explains why a package is released reports `release-trigger`, fixed groups, linked groups, the tag template and pre-major inference as configured when you set them, instead of "(default)".
- `snapshot` works for PyPI packages: their snapshot version and dependents' specs use PEP 440.
- Git errors that came from parsing git's own output now have specific codes and help text, instead of one generic git error code.
- release, release plan, release execute, release artifact-manifest, and release-pr's JSON output now carry schemaVersion, command, and dryRun fields like every other command's JSON output.
- `callisto release-pr verify` accepts `callisto release-pr decide --format json` output as-is again, so the release action can open and update the release PR. 0.9.0 failed with E281.
- Adding a package with the same name in another ecosystem needs no configuration: the existing package keeps its release history, tags and changelog, and new tags use the qualified name (`cargo/foo@1.1.0`). A pre-release cycle started before the new package keeps working. A changeset that names a now-ambiguous `foo` fails with E103 and shows the qualified form to write.
- init now names the exact file it failed to write when a write fails, instead of a pathless error.
- In pre-release mode, packages with the same name in two ecosystems (`cargo/foo`, `npm/foo`) keep separate starting versions in `pre.json` instead of sharing one.
- `callisto release` no longer fails with E167 when GitHub is slow to show a release or asset it just created, uploaded or published; it waits up to a minute.
=== 0.10.2
- Releases that ship artifacts no longer fail with E140: the GitHub CLI that checks attestations and publishes the release keeps its own token instead of running unauthenticated.
=== 0.10.3
- A release rerun adopts a local tag whose message has several paragraphs or a signature, instead of failing while reading it.
- A rerun after a failed tag push now completes the release. A tag that exists on the release commit no longer hides unfinished work: the push, GitHub release and any other missing steps are performed and the receipt is written.
- The generated build-matrix release workflow builds and places napi addons only for packages in the release. An unrelated or misconfigured napi addon no longer adds builds or fails the plan job of a release that does not include it.
=== 0.11.0
- A Python release that stopped partway is completed on rerun. Only the files PyPI lacks are uploaded, and the release counts as published only when both the wheel and the sdist it builds are on the index, so no tag is created for a half-published release. Uploads name their files instead of a dist glob, so a stale dist directory is no longer published.
  
  Breaking: `callisto_graph`'s `registry_argv::pypi_publish_argv` is replaced by `pypi_build_argv` and `pypi_upload_argv`.
- A package that sits behind a symbolic link is now rejected with an error naming it, because Git cannot stage a change to a file beneath a link and the version bump could never be committed. A link that holds no package is ignored, and a link can be skipped by listing it in a `.gitignore` under the workspace root.
- A failed Git lookup is now an error instead of "nothing there". A broken or missing repository used to read as no tags, no such ref, no file at that revision or no matches, so `status` and `version` could plan from the wrong history without saying so. Only Git's own "not found" answer counts as absent now, a tag that is listed but does not resolve to a commit stops the run, and `status` warns once about each tag that matches a package's tag template but is not a version.
- Generated release workflows now install the Python build and upload tools they need. A workspace that publishes to PyPI no longer depends on `twine` being preinstalled on the runner.
- A package published to both Cargo and npm now gets its tag and GitHub release only after both publishes succeed, instead of after the first.
- `callisto add` no longer overwrites an existing changeset when it draws a name that is already taken, and a file Callisto rewrites keeps its permissions (it was left owner-only). A command whose output was cut short because a background process kept its pipes open is now an error instead of a success with empty output. Workspace globs written as `./packages/*` or `packages/*/` now match the same directories as `packages/*`.
- A package published to both Cargo and npm now gets one git tag and one GitHub release. A release that also uploads assets, which failed to plan with a repeated artifact slot, now plans and runs.
- A PyPI token or npm config token that a publish tool echoes in an error is now redacted from the output, like the other registry tokens.
- Callisto now stops, naming the file, when a workspace manifest is malformed instead of guessing which packages it contains. An unreadable or unparseable root `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and a `members`, `exclude`, `workspaces` or `packages` entry that is not a valid list of globs, fail the command; before, they silently admitted every directory, so vendored copies and excluded crates became releasable packages. Locating the workspace root also no longer skips a malformed manifest and settles on a different root.
- **A Cargo dependency declared in several tables is followed and rewritten in each**
  
  A dependency declared more than once, for example in `[dependencies]` and in a `[target.<cfg>.dependencies]` table with different constraints, now cascades to its dependent and is rewritten in every table when the package it names is released. Before, only the first declaration was updated and another one kept a stale constraint. A target declaration whose range still covers the new version now has its lower bound raised, as a plain declaration does. A Python requirement declared more than once, in the project dependencies, in several extras, in Poetry's table or under different markers, is followed and rewritten in each place by its own constraint, so a loose line such as `lib-py>=0.1` has its floor raised to `>=0.2.0` rather than being skipped.
  
  Breaking:
  - `callisto_model`: `DependencyEntry` and `DepEdge` gain a `locator: DepLocator` field naming the table a declaration lives in. `DepLocator` is a `#[non_exhaustive]` enum, `Unspecified` (the default, for npm), `Cargo` or `Python`: build it with `DepLocator::cargo` or `DepLocator::python`. The new `DepContainer` names the Python table. A writer given a locator for another ecosystem returns `DependencyNotFound`.
  - `callisto_manifests`: `Manifest::update_dependency_spec` takes the declaration's `&DepLocator` after the dependency kind.
  - `callisto_graph`: `RewriteKey` gains a `locator` field.
- Yarn classic's `"workspaces": { "packages": [...] }` form is now read for workspace membership, and a root Cargo workspace that cannot be loaded for version inheritance is reported instead of silently dropping the packages that inherit from it.
- Callisto no longer plans a release from a workspace it could only partly read. A package whose manifest cannot be opened (for example a member that inherits its version from a Rust workspace Callisto cannot find) used to keep no publish target and no dependency edges, so it never published and its dependents never cascaded, without a message. Every command now stops with a coded error naming each such manifest.
- A release workflow that builds Python distributions in a job without registry credentials now publishes exactly those files. The generated build-matrix workflow gains a `build-python` job, the manifest records each file's name, size and sha256, and a file PyPI already holds under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release before any upload. Python builds also set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time.
- callisto status now reads a changeset's package names the same way callisto version does. A package named by a non-primary manifest's own name resolves, a qualified name for an ecosystem the package lacks is reported as unknown, and a name that two packages claim is ambiguous, so status --check no longer passes a changeset that version will not consume.
- A release now stops with a clear error when git cannot read the local tag state, for example a corrupt or unreadable repository, or when npm cannot be reached or rejects the version lookup, instead of treating the version as unpublished and attempting to publish or tag. npm 8 and later still report a missing version as unpublished.
- A file Callisto cannot read or look up is now reported instead of treated as missing. An unreadable package manifest, `callisto.toml`, `pre.json` or changelog, a changeset it cannot inspect, and a failed directory sync after a write now stop the command with the file named, where before the package, config, changeset or durability guarantee was silently dropped.
- A release that stops because a provider could not be observed now says why: the HTTP status the registry or forge answered, a failed command, an answer it could not understand, or a timeout.
- `version` now checks every file it is about to write before it writes the first one. A manifest that is missing, unreadable, a directory, in an unwritable folder, or reached through a symbolic link Git cannot stage stops the command with every such file named and nothing changed, instead of failing partway through and leaving some manifests already bumped.
- A pre-release state that records two different starting versions for one package, for example an old bare key and its qualified key, now stops with an error naming both keys and versions instead of silently keeping one.
- A package keeps its release history when its directory moves, when it gains a higher-priority manifest beside a same-named package, or when a same-named sibling is removed. Before, the last release was reported as none, or an older release was chosen over a newer one, so already-released work could be released again.
  
  Breaking:
  - `callisto_graph`: `TagIndex::build` takes the workspace's `&IdentityIndex` after the graph.

oxc-react-docgen-core: patch

Both are gone, from batch extraction and from the watch session's first revision.
== .changeset/child-interface-prop-overrides-parent.md
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

A prop redeclared in a child interface now replaces the inherited one. `interface Child extends Base { x: "a" | "b" }` used to resolve `x` to `Base`'s type, description and parent. An undocumented redeclaration keeps the inherited description, as react-docgen-typescript does.
== .changeset/consolidate-lints-drop-unused-deps.md
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
oxc-react-docgen: patch
oxc-react-docgen-napi: patch
---

Lint policy (`unsafe_code`, clippy `all`) moved from per-crate `#![...]` attributes into a single `[workspace.lints]` table in the workspace root, with each crate opting in via `[lints] workspace = true`. `unsafe_code` is now `"deny"` rather than `"forbid"` — no crate currently uses `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary, but `deny` allows a local `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` override if one is ever genuinely needed there.

== .changeset/dts-cache-concurrent-writes.md
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

Concurrent runs sharing one DTS cache directory — the CLI and the Vite plugin in the same project, or parallel builds — no longer report a spurious `IO_ERROR` "Failed to persist the DTS cache" diagnostic. Every writer used the same temp file name, so the second rename found it already moved. Temp names are now unique per process and write.
== .changeset/fix-rustdoc-errors.md
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
oxc-react-docgen: patch
---

Fixed 7 doc-comment errors that broke `cargo doc` under `-D warnings`: 6 unescaped angle-bracket type names (`Ref<T>`, `RefObject<T>`, `HTMLButtonElement`, etc.) that rustdoc parsed as unclosed HTML tags, and one `[default]` that rustdoc parsed as a broken intra-doc link. No behavior change — fixes how the published crate's documentation renders on docs.rs.
== .changeset/literal-union-bare-members.md
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

String-literal union aliases now report bare member values. A `type Size = "sm" | "md"` alias previously came back with each member already quoted, so serialized output showed `""sm"" | ""md""` and a template literal over the alias expanded to `compact-"sm"`. `undefined` members are dropped (optionality is reported through `required`); a `null` member keeps the alias a plain union, since a string-only literal union can't represent it.

The DTS cache schema version moved to 4 — its key is a content hash and can't detect that the extractor now produces different data for identical input, so existing cache files are discarded rather than served stale.

---
oxc-react-docgen: patch
---

`--format rdt` omits a `children` prop that has no description, matching react-docgen-typescript's default `skipChildrenPropWithoutDoc`. A documented `children` is still emitted, and `--format canonical` is unchanged.

---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch

needs input: I've read the callisto docs and release notes and gone through the recent PRs. Before I change anything I need two decisions from you.

**Corrections to what I said earlier**
- My local `main` is 8 commits behind `origin/main`. `release.yml` and `callisto.toml` there already pin callisto 0.10.0 (PR #20). The 0.8.0 pins I saw are only in the stale checkout, except `ci.yml:166` (`callisto-validate`), which `3f27029` has fixed on origin.
- I can't tell what blocked you on callisto. These are the problems I can see.

**Where the release stands**
- **Nothing has ever been released.** There are no version tags and every package is at `0.1.0`.
  - Callisto releases any package whose current version has no tag.
  - Release PR #22 would bump everything to `0.1.1` and skip `0.1.0`. That PR is a leftover from the changesets.
- **Callisto is behind.** 0.11.0 is out; origin pins 0.10.0, and the `mise` shim on this machine is 0.5.0.
  - 0.10.3 and 0.11.0 add rerun fixes after a failed tag push, builds only for packages in the release, and a stop when a workspace manifest is malformed.
  - 0.9.0 made the release intent schema v4 and publishes napi platform packages with their owner automatically.
  - None of the 0.9–0.11 notes I read look like a breaking change for this config.
- **Unreleased work:** the last 3 weeks of PRs (#12–#25) are almost all fixes.
  - 8 changesets exist, all patches.
  - The only feature commit, `tsc-client` (`1f0be33`), is a new crate with no changeset. It may need `publish = false` or a `callisto.toml` entry.
  - TOON, the LSP scaffold, plugins and the schema export predate those 3 weeks and are covered by no changeset.
- **CI is red.** Both `Coverage` and `Test / Rust` fail on `main` from an `install-action` error, and the 3 newest dependabot PRs fail too. A release shouldn't go out until that is fixed. I haven't diagnosed it.
- **Open PRs:** the dependabot PRs #27, #30, #31 and #32 are open and not merged.
- **Your uncommitted changes:** the `package.json` repo URL fix (`oxc-react-docgen` → `caliper`) matters for npm provenance. Origin's URLs are still the old name, and `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` is on.

**Plan**
1. Pull `origin/main`, then make a branch.
2. Bump the pins to callisto 0.11.0 in `release.yml`, `ci.yml` and the `callisto.toml` comment.
3. Add a changeset for the features and decide how to handle `tsc-client`.
4. Fix CI.
5. Land the URL fix.
6. Run `callisto release --dry-run` and `status --check` on 0.11.0.
7. Merge the release PR.

**Decisions I need**
1. **Version for the first release.** Do you want `0.1.0`, which means deleting the changesets and releasing as-is, or `0.2.0`, which means adding a minor changeset for the feature set? I'd pick `0.2.0` so the changelog describes the features rather than only the fixes.
2. **Your uncommitted tool and package changes.** Do I commit the URL fix and the `.codex`/`.github` hooks on my branch? Last time you didn't pick between the options on `.claude` and `.gemini`, and I'd leave those two out.
Let's follow the plan, yes. Just move forward in versions to avoid problems
Going with 0.2.0. I'll make a worktree off `origin/main` and carry over the URL and hook changes.

content.text: Adding `publish = false` to `tsc-client`, since nothing uses it yet, and writing the minor changeset for the first release.

input.command:
sed -i '' 's/^license.workspace = true$/license.workspace = true\npublish = false/' crates/tsc-client/Cargo.toml; head -8 crates/tsc-client/Cargo.toml; grep -n "^publish" crates/binding/Cargo.toml
cat > .changeset/first-public-release.md <<'EOF'
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: minor
oxc-react-docgen: minor
oxc-react-docgen-napi: minor
"@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin": minor
---

First public release. React component prop extraction on OXC, with no TypeScript `Program` and no type-checking pass: cold extraction across 21 real component libraries in about 50ms and ~2ms for an incremental single-file update.

- `oxc-react-docgen` CLI with `--format canonical | rdt | toon`, `docgen.config.ts` loading, watch mode, and a `schema` subcommand that exports the component metadata as a Draft-07 JSON Schema. `--format rdt` emits a `react-docgen-typescript`-compatible shape (see `MIGRATING.md`); `--format toon` is a token-optimized output for LLM agents.
- Cross-package `.d.ts` resolution with an atomic, bounded on-disk cache, and a plugin system (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) for AST and component resolution hooks.
- NAPI binding and a Vite plugin that expose the canonical format.
- An `lsp` subcommand scaffold with bounded framing and the initialize/shutdown/exit lifecycle. It does not serve prop hovers yet.
EOF

content.text:
The release is half done. `oxc-react-docgen-core` 0.2.0 is on crates.io. Nothing else has published: no other crates, no npm packages, no tags and no GitHub releases.

**What went wrong**
1. **First run (after merging #22):** the `release-candidate` job decided it wasn't a release-PR merge, so `plan`, `build` and `execute` were skipped. Right now the merged-PR lookup and the commit verification both succeed, so it was probably a GitHub timing race. I dispatched the workflow by hand for release-source `71140ca` (the documented recovery).
2. **Dispatched run:** `plan` and all 5 builds passed. `execute` published `oxc-react-docgen-core`, then failed on every retry with E157/E176 when callisto re-checked crates.io.
3. **Cause:** the workflow sets `CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always`. Cargo then prints the `version:` label in `cargo info` wrapped in ANSI escape codes, and callisto's parser for crates.io's answer misses it.
   - I confirmed this by forcing color on locally and dumping the bytes.
   - Without color, callisto would read `cargo info` fine.
   - The same parsing flaw is a bug in callisto 0.11.0 worth reporting upstream.

**The fix:** PR #38 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/38) sets `CARGO_TERM_COLOR: never` for the `execute` job only. I haven't checked its CI yet.

**Next:**
1. Merge #38 once CI is green.
2. I dispatch the recovery again for `71140ca`: `gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha=71140ca619024edb3e39bd770d41193008b67d01`. Callisto will adopt the already-published core crate and publish the rest. Do you want me to run that dispatch as soon as #38 merges?

The release-candidate race may recur on later releases. Re-running the workflow, or dispatching as above, is the workaround.
We need to fix the crate and NPM package names to match caliper right?
Probably yes, and it's cheaper to do now than after publishing. I'm checking what the names would be and whether they're free.

content.text:
needs input: I need the target names, and I'm holding the release until you decide. Nothing more should publish under the old names.

**Why now:** the only thing out under the old name is `oxc-react-docgen-core` 0.2.0 on crates.io. A published crate name can't be removed. You can yank 0.2.0, but the name stays taken. Every other package is still unpublished, so a rename now costs only a rewrite.

**What's free**
- **Crates.io:** `caliper-core`, `caliper-napi` and `caliper-docgen` are free. `caliper` and `caliper-cli` are taken by someone else.
- **npm:** `caliper` is taken. The unscoped names `@caliper/cli` and `@caliper/napi` return 404, but that doesn't mean we own the `@caliper` scope. We'd need to own that npm org.
- **Scope:** about 141 files mention `oxc-react-docgen` or `oxc_react_docgen`. That includes crate and bin names, the npm scope `@oxc-react-docgen`, the napi `binaryName`, the 10 platform packages, `callisto.toml`, `release.yml`, docs, and the `docgen.config.ts` and config-loading text.

**Decisions I need**
1. **Names:** which should the crates and CLI binary be called (e.g. `caliper-core`, `caliper-napi`, and a `caliper` binary from a crate named something other than `caliper-cli`)?
2. **npm scope:** which should it be (`@caliper/*` if you own the org, otherwise `@orin-dx/*`)?

content.text:
PR #39 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/39) renames the crates, the binary and the npm packages, and all 12 CI checks pass. It is not merged and nothing has been published under the new names.

**What changed**
- **Crates:** `caliper-docgen`, `caliper-docgen-core`, `caliper-docgen-napi` and `caliper-docgen-tsc-client`.
- **Binary:** `caliper-docgen`.
- **npm packages:** `@orin-dx/caliper-docgen`, `-napi`, `-vite-plugin` and the platform packages. The napi addon files are `caliper_docgen_napi.*.node`.
- **Other renames:** `callisto.toml`, `release.yml`, docs, snapshots and lockfiles were renamed too. `docs/archive` keeps the old name as history.
- **Stacked on #38:** this branch also contains the `CARGO_TERM_COLOR: never` fix, so merging #39 lands both.
- **Extra CI fix:** the `Install` jobs failed at first because `scripts/verify-install.sh` looked for old tarball names. I fixed it and ran `verify-install` with both pnpm and npm.

I picked these names myself: the `caliper-docgen` binary instead of plain `caliper`, and the `@orin-dx/caliper-docgen-*` npm names. If you want shorter names, say so before merging.

**Release steps**
1. Merge #39.
2. The release-candidate race may recur, so dispatch the workflow by hand: `gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha=<new main SHA>`. The packages are already at 0.2.0, so callisto sees the renamed ones as unreleased and plans a first publish of 0.2.0.
3. After the new `caliper-docgen-core` is out, yank the old `oxc-react-docgen-core` 0.2.0. The old name stays reserved on crates.io.

Tell me when #39 is merged and I'll dispatch and watch the run.

Releasing from `main` isn't possible yet, so I opened PR #40 (https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper/pull/40) to fix that. Nothing is published under the new names.

**Fix:** #40 adds a patch changeset for the six packages, written with `cargo/` and `npm/` prefixes because `caliper-docgen` now exists in both ecosystems. `callisto status --check` shows all six pending as patches and the changeset formatting passes. I haven't checked #40's CI yet.

**Next:**
1. Merge #40. The workflow then opens a release PR bumping the six packages to 0.2.1. That's one version past the 0.2.0 you'd expect, but it avoids a tag clash and skips nothing under the new names.
2. Review that release PR, check its CI, and merge it to publish.
3. If the release-candidate race hits again, I'll dispatch with the merge SHA. Then I yank `oxc-react-docgen-core` 0.2.0.

Yes, callisto should tag, and it tried to. It failed because of a GitHub rule that our delay triggered. Callisto's design is arguably thin here.

**What happened**
- Callisto does create and push the tags itself, using the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`. That works when the release commit is the tip of `main`.
- `219d761` (the #41 release merge) stopped being the tip when you merged dependabot PRs #42 and #43 at 17:15 on 10-20. #42 changed `ci.yml` and `release.yml`.
- GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's `.github/workflows/` files differ from every branch tip. The `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't be granted the `workflows` scope.
- So the stalled run, held up for a day by the token problems, fell into callisto's "recovering an older release" case (E180), which tells you to push the tags yourself.

**Why this is also callisto's gap:** its docs say the manual tag push is the only fix, and the workflow takes no PAT or deploy-key input for tag pushes. A release run that waits on a registry-token fix will hit this whenever `main` moves in the meantime. That's worth an upstream issue.

**What would have avoided it for us:**
- Not merging anything touching `.github/workflows/` while a release is pending. Dependabot actions bumps do exactly that.
- Giving the workflow a PAT or deploy key with `workflows` scope for the tag push. `release.yml` checks out with the default credentials today.

The manual tag push is still the way out now. You can run the commands from my last message, or tell me to go ahead and I'll push the tags and re-run.
We should not be chaning the workflows on publish. WTF.

You're right. Nothing should be able to change the workflows between a release being approved and published, and here dependabot did. Dependabot PRs #42 and #43 merged after the #41 release merge and touched `ci.yml` and `release.yml`. That is what turned a fixable token problem into the E180 tag failure.

**To make it structural, in order of value**
1. **Push tags with a credential that can write workflows.** In the `execute` job, check out `release-source` with a deploy key or PAT that has the `workflows` scope, instead of the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Callisto's own E180 help text names this credential, so E180 stops mattering, even when the release commit isn't the tip. This is the real fix. It needs a deploy key (write access) added to the repo and stored as a secret, which I can't create for you.
2. **Stop dependabot from touching workflows mid-release.** Put the `github-actions` ecosystem on a schedule you control (monthly), or hold those PRs while a release PR is open. This is cheap, but it relies on discipline.
3. **Upstream:** file an issue on callisto asking for a tag-push credential input and a warning when the release commit isn't the tip.

content.text:
Callisto's own repo has no special mechanism. Its release workflow uses the same setup we do, and the same failure would hit it if `main` moved mid-release.

**How callisto does it** (`callisto-release.yml` at `callisto@0.11.0`):
- The `execute` job checks out the release source with `persist-credentials: true`, and callisto pushes tags with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. That is identical to our `execute`.
- There's no PAT, deploy key or workflow-file guard. Its dependabot config is the same weekly, 7-day cooldown `github-actions` group as ours.
- Its releases work because they run to completion within minutes of the release PR merging, while the release commit is still the tip of `main`.

**What we did wrong**
1. **Held the release open for about a day.** The first run's candidate check misfired, then the registry tokens were missing, then the secrets weren't shared with the repo. Meanwhile `main` kept moving.
2. **Merged workflow-changing PRs during that window.** Dependabot PRs #42 and #43 merged at 17:15 on 10-20 and changed `ci.yml` and `release.yml`. That broke the one condition the `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push depends on.
3. **Ran the recovery as "re-run failed jobs."** That re-ran against the original release commit, which was no longer a branch tip, so it hit the E180 case.
4. **Missed the token risk at setup.** I checked that the secrets existed but not their visibility or whether the tokens could publish a brand-new crate. All the delays came from there. I should have flagged it before the first publish attempt.

A deploy key would still protect us from this, but it isn't how callisto avoids it. If you'd rather keep things like callisto, the practical rule is: don't merge anything that touches `.github/workflows/` while a release is pending.

content.text:
Yes. The crates are missing most of the metadata that callisto's have.

**Rust crates** (`caliper-docgen`, `-core`, `-napi`, `-tsc-client`)
- **Callisto sets at the workspace level:** `repository`, `homepage`, `documentation` (docs.rs), `keywords`, `categories`. Each crate inherits them and also sets `readme = "README.md"`, and has its own README, LICENSE and CHANGELOG in the crate directory.
- **Ours:** each crate has only `name`, `description`, `version`, `edition` and `license`. There's no `repository`, `homepage`, `documentation`, `keywords`, `categories` or `readme`, and no per-crate README or LICENSE.
- **`authors`:** the workspace sets it, but no crate inherits it.
- **Fallout:** the publish log warned `manifest has no documentation, homepage or repository`. crates.io shows no repo or docs link and no README for `caliper-docgen-core` and `caliper-docgen`.

**npm packages**
- `package.json` has only the `repository.url`, with no `directory`.
- There's no `homepage`, `bugs` or `keywords`, and no README in the package, so the npm pages will be blank.
- The CLI `description` is a long internal note, not a one-line summary.

**Consequence:** metadata is fixed per published version. Both crates are already out as 0.2.1 without it, and the npm packages will be too if attempt 4 publishes them. Fixing it needs another patch release (0.2.2).

**The fix is one PR:**
- Workspace `repository`, `homepage`, `documentation`, `keywords` and `categories`, inherited by every crate.
- Per-crate `readme` and README files, plus a LICENSE copy in each published crate.
- npm `homepage`, `bugs`, `keywords` and `repository.directory`, a README per package, and a one-line CLI description.
- A patch changeset.

I'd write the READMEs short and factual from `README.md` and `docs/STATUS.md`. Before merging, wait for attempt 4 to settle. Do you want me to go ahead?

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-run the failed callisto execute job each time the only failure is npm's new-package propagation lag (E157).
# Stops on success, or on any failure that is not E157.
set -uo pipefail
RUN=39356498287
OUT=/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/drive-release.log
: > "$OUT"
say() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%H:%M:%S)" "$*" | tee -a "$OUT"; }

for i in $(seq 1 16); do
  while [ "$(gh run view $RUN --json status --jq .status)" != completed ]; do sleep 15; done
  concl=$(gh run view $RUN --json conclusion --jq .conclusion)
  attempt=$(gh run view $RUN --json attempt --jq .attempt)
  say "attempt $attempt: $concl"
  if [ "$concl" = success ]; then say "RELEASE COMPLETE"; exit 0; fi
  job=$(gh run view $RUN --json jobs --jq '.jobs[]|select(.conclusion=="failure")|.databaseId')
  log=$(gh run view --job "$job" --log 2>&1 | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g')
  if ! printf '%s' "$log" | grep -q '^.*E157'; then
    say "STOP: failure is not E157"
    printf '%s' "$log" | grep -E "^.{0,80}(E[0-9]{3}|npm error|  × |^error)" | tail -12 | cut -c1-240 | tee -a "$OUT"
    exit 1
  fi
  pkg=$(printf '%s' "$log" | grep -oE 'registry reported `[^`]+`' | head -1 | sed -E 's/registry reported `//; s/`$//')
  say "waiting for registry to show $pkg"
  tries=0
  while [ $tries -lt 60 ]; do
    if npm view "$pkg" version 2>/dev/null | grep -q '[0-9]'; then break; fi
    tries=$((tries+1)); sleep 15
  done
  say "$pkg visible (tries=$tries), re-running"
  gh run rerun $RUN --failed
  sleep 20
done
say "STOP: iteration cap reached"
exit 1

> **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete.

## Why

`react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system that takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish.

OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass:

- **Cold extraction, 21 real component libraries:** 50ms ([full breakdown](docs/benchmarks.md))
- **Incremental single-file update:** ~2ms — react-docgen-typescript has no equivalent API; every edit re-pays the full cold cost

The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet.

## Install

> Not yet on npm. No prebuilt per-platform binaries exist yet — build from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper
cd caliper
pnpm install
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi run build:napi   # builds the native addon for your platform
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin build
```

Use `pnpm run build:napi`, not a bare `cargo build` — it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s loader expects it.

Migrating off `react-docgen-typescript`? See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) for what's compatible today.

```ts

import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })],
})
```

# caliper-docgen

React component prop extraction, powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust, with no TypeScript compiler program and no type-checking pass.

```bash
npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen
npx caliper-docgen extract --src src --format rdt
```

- `--format canonical | rdt | toon`: `rdt` emits a `react-docgen-typescript`-compatible shape, `toon` a token-optimized one for LLM agents.
- `watch` re-extracts on change. `schema` prints the JSON Schema for the output.
- Reads `docgen.config.ts` from the project root.

This package is a thin wrapper that runs the prebuilt binary for your platform (`caliper-docgen-darwin-arm64`, `-linux-x64-gnu`, and so on, pulled in as optional dependencies). All behavior lives in the Rust CLI.

Docs, benchmarks and migration notes from `react-docgen-typescript`: https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper

# caliper-docgen-core

Core library for [caliper-docgen](https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper): extracts React component props from TypeScript with [OXC](https://oxc.rs). No TypeScript compiler program and no type-checking pass, so a cold run over 21 real component libraries takes about 50ms.

Pipeline: parse files in parallel, merge the symbol data, resolve each component's props, return the extraction output. Whenever it degrades it emits a `Diagnostic` rather than failing silently.

This crate is pure extraction logic: no terminal output, no async. The command-line tool is [`caliper-docgen`](https://crates.io/crates/caliper-docgen), and the Node bindings are [`caliper-docgen-napi`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/caliper-docgen-napi).

Docs: https://docs.rs/caliper-docgen-core. Architecture notes and known gaps: https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper

License: AGPL-3.0-or-later.

# caliper-docgen

Command-line React component prop extraction, powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs).

```bash
cargo install caliper-docgen
caliper-docgen extract --src src --format rdt
```

Yes, that matches how callisto is set up, and caliper is currently different. I haven't changed anything; this is the call to make first.

**Callisto's licensing**
- **Copyright:** `LICENSE` is FSL-1.1-MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Gabriel Castro (Orin DX)".
- **Split:** the workspace is `FSL-1.1-MIT` (becomes MIT two years after each version's release), except `callisto-model`, which is plain `MIT`.
- **Why the split:** it's the library other code depends on.

**Caliper's licensing**
- Everything is `AGPL-3.0-or-later`: the workspace `Cargo.toml`, 13 `package.json` files, `deny.toml`, the root README, and the READMEs I just wrote in #45.

**What to know before switching**
- **Published versions:** 0.2.1 is already out under AGPL on crates.io and npm. That's permanent for those versions, so the first FSL release would be 0.2.2.
- **Relicensing:** this is fine if you're the sole copyright holder. Check that no outside contributions exist beyond dependabot (the workspace `authors` field says "contributors", but I haven't audited commits).
- **Adoption:** FSL isn't OSI open source, and it bars competing commercial use. For a tool design systems will install into their toolchains, that may matter. AGPL has its own friction for companies.

**My suggestion:** mirror callisto. `caliper-docgen-core` and the npm packages that expose it become `MIT`, like `callisto-model`, and the CLI, napi binding and Vite plugin become `FSL-1.1-MIT`. Say if you'd rather make everything FSL, or everything MIT.

**What it touches:** `LICENSE` (copied into the published crates), the workspace and per-crate `license`, all `package.json` files, the READMEs, `deny.toml`, and the root README's license section. I'd put it in its own PR or fold it into #45, since both ship in 0.2.2 anyway.

Crate map, data flow, and the invariants every change must preserve.

--- ## Invariants 1. **Safe Rust only.** `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide. 2. **License boundary.** `callisto-model` is MIT and must never depend on an FSL-1.1-MIT crate. Every other crate is FSL-1.1-MIT. Check with `grep -H "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml`. 3. **Format-preserving manifest edits.** `Cargo.toml` goes through `toml_edit`'s CST; `package.json` is fingerprinted for indent style and line endings before a `serde_json` (`preserve_order`) round trip. No regex or line-based edits to manifests. 4. **One file-write primitive, capability-gated.** `callisto_model::atomic::atomic_write` (`NamedTempFile` in the target's own directory, `fsync`, `persist` via `fs::rename`, then `fsync` the parent and grandparent directories) is the only way file content is written; deletions and directory creation use `std::fs`. It takes `&ApplyPermit`, a token with a private field that only `ApplyPermit::granted_unless_dry_run(dry_run)` can construct, returning `None` on a dry run. A write path that forgets to check `--dry-run` has no permit to pass and fails to compile. 5. **System Git only.** All VCS reads and writes shell out to the user's `git` binary (`callisto_model::vcs`), so Callisto sees exactly the repository, config, and identity Git itself does. No embedded Git implementation. 6. **User-facing errors are diagnosable.** Every error surfaced to a user derives `miette::Diagnostic` with a stable code and, where the fix isn't obvious from the message, `help` text. A wrapper around another crate's error (for example `GraphError::Config`) is `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and declares no code of its own, so the inner code reaches the user. React component prop extraction powered by [OXC](https://oxc.rs). Parses TypeScript natively in Rust — no TypeScript compiler program, no type-checking pass, no startup tax. > **Status:** Core extraction, NAPI bindings, Vite plugin, CLI, and `docgen.config.ts` loading are complete. ## Why `react-docgen-typescript` spins up a full TypeScript `Program` to extract props. On a mid-size design system that takes seconds — enough to noticeably delay Storybook startup and make HMR feel sluggish. OXC parses each file in parallel with no type-checking pass: - **Cold extraction, 21 real component libraries:** 50ms ([full breakdown](docs/benchmarks.md)) - **Incremental single-file update:** ~2ms — react-docgen-typescript has no equivalent API; every edit re-pays the full cold cost The CLI can emit an RDT-compatible shape via `--format rdt` (see [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)). The Vite plugin and NAPI binding currently expose this tool's own canonical format only — not a drop-in RDT replacement at that layer yet. ## Install ```bash npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen # CLI, with the prebuilt binary for your platform npm install --save-dev caliper-docgen-vite-plugin # Vite plugin cargo install caliper-docgen # CLI from crates.io ``` To build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper cd caliper pnpm install pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi run build:napi # builds the native addon for your platform pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin build ``` Use `pnpm run build:napi`, not a bare `cargo build` — it invokes `napi build`, which places the compiled addon exactly where `packages/napi/index.js`'s loader expects it. Migrating off `react-docgen-typescript`? See [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) for what's compatible today. ## Vite plugin ```ts // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from 'vite' import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react' import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'] })], }) ``` Metadata is available on the `virtual:caliper-docgen` module and pushed via HMR as components change: ```ts import docgen from 'virtual:caliper-docgen' docgen.components['Button'].props // { // variant: { // type: { kind: 'literalUnion', members: ['default', 'destructive', 'outline'], hasDefault: true }, // required: false, // defaultValue: { value: '"default"', computed: false }, // description: '', // }, // ... // } ``` ## CLI A single Rust binary (`crates/cli`) — argument parsing, output formatting, and `--format rdt`/`--format storybook` serialization all live there. `caliper-docgen` (once published) is a thin npm wrapper that execs the platform-appropriate compiled binary — no reimplemented logic, so there's exactly one place CLI behavior can drift. ```bash # Once published: npx caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # From source today: ./target/release/caliper-docgen (after cargo build --release) # One-shot extraction caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --out docgen.json # Inspect a single file caliper-docgen inspect src/components/Button.tsx # Watch mode caliper-docgen watch --src src/ # Shell completions caliper-docgen completions zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_caliper-docgen # Full HTML attribute expansion instead of the default curated subset caliper-docgen extract --src src/ --html-attributes full ``` Settings can also live in `docgen.config.ts` (`srcDirs`, `htmlAttributes`, `reactVersion`, `crossPackage`, and more — see `crates/cli/src/config.rs` for the full schema) instead of CLI flags. ## Output shape ```json { "components": { "Button": { "displayName": "Button", "filePath": "src/components/Button.tsx", "props": { "variant": { "type": { "kind": "literalUnion", "members": ["default", "destructive", "outline"], "hasDefault": true }, "required": false, "defaultValue": { "value": "\"default\"", "computed": false }, "description": "Visual style variant.", "tags": {} } }, "inheritance": [ { "typeName": "ButtonHTMLAttributes", "htmlElement": "button", "omitted": [], "totalProps": 147 } ], "notableInherited": { "onClick": { "type": { "kind": "eventHandler", "eventType": "MouseEvent" }, ... }, "disabled": { "type": { "kind": "boolean" }, ... } }, "discriminantProp": null } }, "diagnostics": [], "stats": { "filesParsed": 3, "durationMs": 12, "dtsCacheHits": 2, ... } } ``` ## Supported patterns | Pattern | Example | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | Function components | `function Button(props: ButtonProps)` | | Arrow components | `const Button = (props: ButtonProps) => ...` | | `React.forwardRef` | `forwardRef(...)` | | HOC-wrapped | `styled(Base)` | | Interface inheritance | `interface ButtonProps extends HTMLAttributes` | | Intersection aliases | `type ButtonProps = BaseProps & { variant?: string }` | | `Omit` / `Pick` | `type ButtonProps = Omit` | | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` | | `VariantProps` | `VariantProps` (CVA / TV / PandaCSS) | | Discriminated unions | MUI-style `variant: 'filled' \| 'outlined' \| 'standard'` | | JSDoc tags | `@description`, `@default`, `@deprecated`, `@internal` | ##
