"""Turn the open PRs into one linear stack: merge each PR's predecessor into it, push (fast-forward), retarget its base.

Usage: restack.py START_INDEX [--dry-run]. Stops at the first merge conflict, leaving it for manual resolution; rerun
from that index once it's committed.
"""
import subprocess, sys

GIT = '/usr/bin/git'
REPO = 'orin-dx/caliper'
ORDER = [  # (pr, branch); the first one's base is main
    (98, 'ci/callisto-0.12'), (102, 'docs/oxfmt-073-toml'), (100, 'test/doctest-seal'),
    (97, 'fix/resolver-groundwork'), (99, 'feat/namespace-reexports'), (101, 'feat/component-props-of-typeof'),
    (103, 'fix/function-type-text'), (104, 'fix/alias-display'), (105, 'perf/shared-props'),
    (106, 'docs/adr-dependency-types'), (107, 'feat/load-dependency-types'), (109, 'feat/collapse-inherited-props'),
    (121, 'fix/jsdoc-one-line-function'), (122, 'fix/dom-handler-overwrite'), (123, 'fix/zod-infer-unwrap'),
    (110, 'fix/factory-payload-props'), (112, 'fix/called-helpers-are-not-components'), (113, 'feat/exported-flag'),
    (115, 'fix/rdt-file-path'), (111, 'feat/watch-rebuild-on-config'), (114, 'feat/session-ensure-fresh'),
    (116, 'ci/size-normalized-gates'), (118, 'docs/status-and-ts7'), (108, 'spike/napi-in-worker-threads'),
    (117, 'feat/storybook-provider'), (119, 'feat/storybook-vite-docgen'), (120, 'chore/remove-storybook-format'),
]


def run(*args, check=True):
    out = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and out.returncode != 0:
        sys.exit(f'FAILED: {" ".join(args)}\n{out.stdout}{out.stderr}')
    return out


start = int(sys.argv[1])
dry = '--dry-run' in sys.argv
run(GIT, 'fetch', '-q', 'origin')
for index in range(start, len(ORDER)):
    pr, branch = ORDER[index]
    base = 'main' if index == 0 else ORDER[index - 1][1]
    # The local branch must not hold commits the remote lacks before it's reset to the remote.
    if run(GIT, 'rev-parse', '--verify', '-q', branch, check=False).returncode == 0:
        ahead = run(GIT, 'rev-list', '--count', f'origin/{branch}..{branch}').stdout.strip()
        if ahead != '0':
            sys.exit(f'{branch} has {ahead} local commits not on origin; stopping')
    run(GIT, 'checkout', '-q', '-B', branch, f'origin/{branch}')
    merge_from = 'origin/main' if index == 0 else base
    merged = run(GIT, 'merge', '--no-edit', '-q', merge_from, check=False)
    if merged.returncode != 0:
        conflicts = run(GIT, 'diff', '--name-only', '--diff-filter=U').stdout.split()
        print(f'[{index}] #{pr} {branch}: CONFLICT merging {merge_from}: {conflicts}')
        sys.exit(2)
    changed = run(GIT, 'rev-list', '--count', f'origin/{branch}..{branch}').stdout.strip()
    print(f'[{index}] #{pr} {branch} <- {base}: merged ({changed} new commits)')
    if dry:
        continue
    if changed != '0':
        run(GIT, 'push', '-q', 'origin', branch)
    run('gh', 'pr', 'edit', str(pr), '--repo', REPO, '--base', base)
print('done')

"""Resolve conflict blocks where one side is empty by keeping the other; report files with two-sided blocks left."""
import re, sys

BLOCK = re.compile(r'<<<<<<< [^\n]*\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n', re.S)
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    text = open(path).read()
    left = []

    def keep(m):
        ours, theirs = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        if not ours.strip():
            return theirs
        if not theirs.strip():
            return ours
        left.append(m.group(0))
        return m.group(0)

    text = BLOCK.sub(keep, text)
    open(path, 'w').write(text)
    print(f'{path}: {"resolved" if not left else f"{len(left)} two-sided block(s) left"}')

"""Resolve the first conflict block of a file.

Usage: resolve.py FILE ours|theirs
       resolve.py FILE both GLUE        (ours + GLUE + theirs; GLUE uses \\n escapes)
       resolve.py FILE with TEXT_FILE   (replace the block with TEXT_FILE's contents)
"""
import re, sys

path, mode = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
text = open(path).read()
m = re.search(r'<<<<<<< [^\n]*\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n', text, re.S)
if not m:
    sys.exit(f'{path}: no conflict block')
ours, theirs = m.group(1), m.group(2)
if mode == 'ours':
    new = ours
elif mode == 'theirs':
    new = theirs
elif mode == 'both':
    new = ours + sys.argv[3].encode().decode('unicode_escape') + theirs
elif mode == 'with':
    new = open(sys.argv[3]).read()
else:
    sys.exit(f'unknown mode {mode}')
open(path, 'w').write(text[:m.start()] + new + text[m.end():])
print(f'{path}: resolved ({mode}); {text.count("<<<<<<< ") - 1} block(s) left')

docs/architecture/napi-binding.md-28-
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md-29-Every entry point wraps its real body in `caliper_docgen_core::panic_guard::contain_panic(label, closure)`. This is not incidental defense — it is a deliberate, documented design decision (`docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md`) with a specific and non-obvious shape:
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md-30-
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md-31-- **The `spawn_blocking`-wrapped entry points** (`extract_all`, `initialize_session`, `extract_file_incremental`, `ensure_fresh`) put `contain_panic` **inside** the `spawn_blocking` closure, not around it. Before ADR 0005, these three were only accidentally panic-safe: `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` happens to catch an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not because anyone decided panic-safety belonged there. Wrapping in `contain_panic` too makes the guarantee a designed one, converts the panic into a `Diagnostic`-derived `napi::Error` message instead of an opaque `JoinError`, and stops being contingent on tokio's internals never changing.
docs/architecture/napi-binding.md-32-- **`create_session` and `close_session` get `contain_panic` directly**, with no `spawn_blocking` at all, because they run synchronously on the thread the JS call arrived on. Before ADR 0005 these two had **zero** panic protection — not even the accidental kind — documented as an open, unconfirmed risk in `docs/edge-cases.md` P1-9 ("_(Needs verification, not confirmed)_... Whether a panic here crashes the Node process depends on whether napi-rs's codegen auto-wraps in `catch_unwind`"). ADR 0005 closes that gap directly rather than relying on napi-rs's opt-in `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` attribute (considered and rejected in the ADR's "Alternatives considered" section, in favor of one mechanism — `contain_panic` — shared across rayon, plugin hooks, and FFI instead of two different ones). **Note for future readers of `docs/edge-cases.md`: P1-9 as currently written is stale** — it describes a state ADR 0005 has since fixed; it should be marked resolved rather than open next time that document is touched.

docs/architecture/napi-binding.md-36-## Why this crate's panic discipline is higher-stakes than `crates/cli`'s

docs/architecture/napi-binding.md-38-`panic_guard::contain_panic` is shared code — the same function backs rayon `.map()` closures in `pipeline/mod.rs`, `DocgenPlugin` hook calls in `plugin.rs`, and all six entry points here. But the failure mode on the other side of an _uncaught_ panic differs by boundary. `crates/cli` is a standalone binary process: an uncaught panic there kills one CLI invocation, and the OS process boundary means nothing else is affected. This crate is a `cdylib` loaded **in-process** into a long-running Node.js server (a Vite dev server, per the doc comments on `create_session`/`initialize_session`/`close_session` referencing `configResolved`/`configureServer`/`buildEnd`). An uncaught Rust panic crossing the FFI boundary here does not fail one call — it is undefined behavior at best and a hard crash of the entire Node process at worst, taking down every other request the dev server was serving. That asymmetry is why `contain_panic` at this boundary is load-bearing in a way it is only "good hygiene" for `crates/cli`: bypass it here and the blast radius is the whole host process, not one invocation.

A change to a tsconfig, `package.json` or lockfile in or above `srcDirs` (installing a package, editing `paths`) re-extracts everything and arrives as an ordinary update event.

Pass `loadDependencies: true` to resolve the types your props import from installed packages; by default they stay named references.

In `vite build --watch`, a change to any file under `srcDirs`, or to that configuration, triggers a rebuild, even one no bundle module imports. A build fails if extraction fails.

## Storybook without the docgen server

On Storybook 10, or Storybook 11 with `features.docgenServer: false`, Storybook reads each component's `__docgenInfo`. With `injectDocgenInfo`, the plugin assigns it from the session, in react-docgen-typescript's shape, and an edit re-transforms every module whose components it changed. Turn off Storybook's own docgen plugin so it doesn't overwrite the assignments:

```ts
// .storybook/main.ts
import type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { caliperDocgen } from 'caliper-docgen-vite-plugin'

const config: StorybookConfig = {
  framework: '@storybook/react-vite',
  stories: ['../src/**/*.stories.tsx'],
  typescript: { reactDocgen: false },
  viteFinal: (config) => ({
    ...config,
    plugins: [...(config.plugins ?? []), caliperDocgen({ srcDirs: ['src'], injectDocgenInfo: true })],
  }),
}
export default config
```

Each assignment sits in a `try`, so a component the module can't reach by name (an anonymous default export) keeps no docs instead of failing. On Storybook 11 with the docgen server on, use `caliper-docgen-storybook` instead.

83	
84	**Locked design decision:** `rdt::docgen_info` hardcodes `"methods": []` unconditionally rather than omitting the field or computing it. content.text: The test's 3-second CPU window opens only after a change has gone through the watcher, so startup isn't the cause. Measuring the idle CPU of the actual binary locally at finer resolution.

input.content:
"""Idle CPU of `caliper-docgen watch` after one change, sampled finely with psutil-free `ps -o time`."""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time

binary = sys.argv[1]
src = tempfile.mkdtemp()
widget = os.path.join(src, 'Widget.tsx')
open(widget, 'w').write('export function Widget(props: { label: string }) { return null; }\n')
proc = subprocess.Popen([binary, 'watch', src], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
time.sleep(2)
open(widget, 'a').write('// 1\n')
time.sleep(1)


def cpu():
    out = subprocess.run(['ps', '-o', 'time=', '-p', str(proc.pid)], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    m, s = out.split(':')
    return int(m) * 60 + float(s)


for _ in range(int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 5):
    before = cpu()
    time.sleep(1)
    print(f'{cpu() - before:.2f}s CPU per 1s idle')
proc.kill()

Yes, all three fail, and the cause in #119 and #120 is now fixed.

**1. Vite integration test (#119, #120): fixed.** When I resolved #117's merge conflicts, I put `filePath` into `__docgenInfo`, so the test's `Button` had 6 keys instead of 5. `filePath` now appears only in `--format rdt`, which is what #115 intended. I pushed the fix on #117 and merged it forward into #119 and #120. Locally, all 7 integration tests pass and lint is clean; CI is rerunning.

**2. `watch_stays_idle_when_stdin_is_not_a_terminal` (#116, #118, #108, #119): not fixed, cause unconfirmed.**
- On Linux CI, the idle watch process used about 2s of CPU in a 3s window; the limit is 2s.
- It started with #111 (`feat/watch-rebuild-on-config`). It failed on 5 of the 8 restacked runs from #111 upward and never on branches below it. #116 and #118 change no Rust code.
- On macOS the same binary uses 0.00s of CPU per idle second, and the Docker daemon isn't running, so I couldn't reproduce it on Linux.
- My leading theory:
  - #111 adds any `package.json`, tsconfig or lockfile found above the source dirs to watchexec's watch set.
  - On Linux, watchexec then also watches each such file's parent directory.
  - If one of those files sits in `/tmp` or `/` on the CI runner, the watcher would receive an event for every temp dir that parallel tests create and delete. That would make the CPU use depend on timing, which matches the intermittent failures.
  - This is unproven: I haven't confirmed such a file exists on the runner.

Deciding the fix needs one Linux run. A one-off CI step that lists those files above the test's temp dir would settle it. Tell me if you want me to push it on a scratch branch.

input.content:
name: Diag watch idle CPU

on:
  push:
    branches: [scratch/watch-idle-diag]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  diag:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      - run: sudo apt-get install -y strace >/dev/null
      - run: cargo build -p caliper-docgen
      - name: Measure
        run: |
          set -x
          echo "TMPDIR=${TMPDIR:-unset}"
          ls -la / /tmp | grep -Ei 'json|lock' || echo "no configs in / or /tmp"
          src=$(mktemp -d)
          printf 'export function Widget(props: { label: string }) { return null; }\n' > "$src/Widget.tsx"
          ./target/debug/caliper-docgen watch "$src" < /dev/null > "$RUNNER_TEMP/watch.log" 2>&1 &
          pid=$!
          sleep 4
          echo '// 1' >> "$src/Widget.tsx"
          sleep 2
          ticks() { awk '{print $14 + $15}' "/proc/$pid/stat"; }
          echo "== idle, no churn (ticks per second, 100 = one core)"
          for i in 1 2 3 4; do a=$(ticks); sleep 1; echo "$(( $(ticks) - a ))"; done
          echo "== while other processes create and delete dirs in /tmp"
          ( for i in $(seq 1 3000); do d=$(mktemp -d); rmdir "$d"; done ) &
          churn=$!
          for i in 1 2 3 4; do a=$(ticks); sleep 1; echo "$(( $(ticks) - a ))"; done
          wait "$churn" || true
          echo "== strace summary over 3s idle"
          sudo timeout 3 strace -c -f -p "$pid" 2>&1 | head -25 || true
          echo "== threads"
          ls "/proc/$pid/task" | wc -l
          for t in /proc/$pid/task/*; do echo "$(cat $t/comm) $(awk '{print $14+$15}' $t/stat)"; done | sort -k2 -n | tail -8
          echo "== watch output"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/watch.log"
          kill "$pid"

CI now passes on all 27 PRs in the stack (#98 → #120). The four that were still failing (#116, #118, #108, #120) all had the same cause, a real bug in `caliper-docgen watch` on Linux rather than a flaky test.

**The bug:** on Linux, saving one file sent watch into an endless loop.
- Applying a change reads the file, and Linux's file watcher reports that read as an event, which watch then applied again.
- The idle process used about 1.2 CPU cores and opened the file around 600 times a second, printing the same component update over and over.
- macOS doesn't report file reads as events, so it never happened locally.

**The fix:** watch now ignores read events. It's on #111 with a unit test covering both kinds of event, and I merged it into the 8 PRs above it.

**How it was checked:** on a Linux CI runner, one edit now produces one update and the process then uses no CPU. Locally, all tests pass except `a_signal_restores_the_terminal_mode_the_session_changed`, the known flaky test. It fails only on macOS when tests run in parallel, passed 5 of 5 times on its own, and hasn't failed in CI. Lint is clean.

The three false components in the 142-component precision sample were functions that look like components (PascalCase, a typed first parameter, returning JSX) but are used as functions: `IndexedAccess(type)` and `ObjectType(type)` in spectrum's docs, called directly, and `TableDropIndicatorWrapper(props, ref)`, handed over as `{render: TableDropIndicatorWrapper}`.

## Rule

The extractor now counts how each name is used in its file (`extractor/uses.rs`): references, calls (`Name(...)`), and renders (a JSX tag, or the first argument of `createElement` or a component wrapper). A non-exported candidate is skipped, with a `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` diagnostic giving the reason, when:

- every reference is a call: it's a helper; or
- it takes a second parameter (a function component takes only props) and is never rendered: it's a render callback.

Exported functions (including `export default function`) are never dropped: they may be rendered elsewhere. A function that's also passed as a value (`items.map(Row)`) or rendered once is kept.

input.content:
Stacked on #120.

`a_signal_restores_the_terminal_mode_the_session_changed` failed about every other run on macOS under parallel load: `left: None, right: Some(0)`, so a signal killed the process instead of watch handling it.

The test sent SIGTERM once the terminal was in raw mode. The keyboard thread sets raw mode before watchexec installs its signal handlers, so under load SIGTERM could arrive first and take the default action. The test now also waits until watch reports a file change, as the non-terminal signal tests already do, which proves the handlers are up.

## Verify

- `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen`: 6 consecutive full runs, 148 of 148 pass each time (it failed in about half before).

# 0010. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23

## Context

The pipeline parses only the project's own files, `@types/react` (full HTML-attribute mode) and TypeScript's lib files. An import into `node_modules` resolves to a path, but nothing parses that file, so a prop typed by a package (`ClosableType`, `OnValueChange`, a Radix primitive's props) stays an unresolved name. With dependencies installed, unresolved types sat at 116 (antd), 323 (chakra), 586 (spectrum) and about 1,000 (shadcn), and RDT expanded what we couldn't.

Loading whole files along imports is the wrong unit. The file-level closures of the five benchmark projects hold 150–6,218 files, and the cost is the file count: about 25 µs per file, almost all of it opening the file (18 threads open only 1.7× faster than one on macOS), against 418 MB/s for parsing. A prototype that loads only the files declaring a name the project uses read 39–833 files warm instead of 150–6,218.

## Decision

Behind `PipelineOptions::load_dependencies` (off by default), a phase before `NamedTypeIndex::build` loads the dependency declarations the project's type positions name, transitively, and nothing else.

- **Demands, not files.** A demand is a package specifier and an imported name used in a type position (a type reference, `typeof X`, heritage, a type argument). A loaded declaration's own references become new demands. One rayon scope runs them; each declaring file is claimed once, and results are keyed by file and name, so the outcome does not depend on scheduling.
- **A separate, shared layer.** Loaded declarations live in a `DependencyLayer` behind an `Arc`, with its own type index and import map. Project lookups fall back to it; keys are file paths, so the layers never collide. Watch revisions share it; an edit that adds a demand gets a new layer version with the new declarations added, never a copy of the project's data.
- **Precedence:** project declaration, then a known shortcut (`VariantProps`, `SxProps`, `HTMLChakraProps`, …), then a dependency declaration, then a builtin. The shortcuts exist because the real declarations are conditional types the structural resolver can't evaluate; a loaded declaration must not replace them.
- **Values stay out of the output.** A dependency's components go into a value index that `ComponentProps<typeof X>` and `typeof Pkg.Root` consult; they are never emitted. Dependency enums never become public output enums or feed the bare-name enum index.
- **Every unresolved demand is reported** on the component whose resolution reached it: a package with no types, an unresolvable specifier, a name the package doesn't export.

## Consequences

- In the experiment that proved this design (`exp/dependency-types`), unresolved types fell to 8 (mantine), 26 (chakra), 82 (shadcn), 58 (antd) and 172 (spectrum), for 2–29 ms of loading on a warm index.
- Props that reach large shared types grow sharply (chakra 560 → 398,910 in its own repo), which is why 0012 collapses large dependency sources and why resolved props are shared, not copied (#105).
- A watch edit that adds a package import costs one index lookup and a few files (under 1 ms in the prototype); `node_modules`, `package.json` and tsconfig changes still need `rebuild()`.
- `declare module` augmentations, `declare global` and `node:*` ambient modules are not loaded yet; a name only they provide stays unresolved, with a diagnostic.
- The TypeScript backend (0006, 0007) gets fewer incomplete components to handle; both now report parents inside `node_modules`.

"""Count props whose type text or default changed between two caliper binaries, per corpus, with examples, and time
both. Usage: type_diff.py BEFORE AFTER [--show N]"""
import json, subprocess, sys, time

BEFORE, AFTER = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
SHOW = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--show') + 1]) if '--show' in sys.argv else 4
B = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp'
CORPORA = [
    ('mantine', f'{B}/bench-corpus/mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src'),
    ('chakra', f'{B}/bench-corpus/chakra-ui/packages/react/src'),
    ('shadcn', f'{B}/bench-corpus/shadcn-ui/apps/v4'),
    ('antd', f'{B}/bench-corpus/ant-design/components'),
    ('spectrum', f'{B}/bench-corpus/react-spectrum/packages'),
]


def run(binary, src):
    out = json.loads(subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json'], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout)
    props = out.get('props', {})
    result = {}
    for key, c in out['components'].items():
        for name, p in c['props'].items():
            p = props.get(p, p) if isinstance(p, str) else p
            result[(key, name)] = (json.dumps(p.get('type')), json.dumps(p.get('defaultValue')))
    return result


def best_ms(binary, src):
    best = None
    for _ in range(5):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json'], capture_output=True, check=True)
        elapsed = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
        best = elapsed if best is None else min(best, elapsed)
    return best


print('| Corpus | Types changed | Defaults changed | ms before → after (best of 5) |')
print('| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |')
details = []
for name, src in CORPORA:
    a, b = run(BEFORE, src), run(AFTER, src)
    common = a.keys() & b.keys()
    types = sorted(k for k in common if a[k][0] != b[k][0])
    defaults = sorted(k for k in common if a[k][1] != b[k][1])
    print(f'| {name} | {len(types)} | {len(defaults)} | {best_ms(BEFORE, src):.0f} → {best_ms(AFTER, src):.0f} |')
    for k in types[:SHOW]:
        details.append(f'{name} type {k[0]}.{k[1]}: {a[k][0][:110]} → {b[k][0][:140]}')
    for k in defaults[:SHOW]:
        details.append(f'{name} default {k[0]}.{k[1]}: {a[k][1]} → {b[k][1]}')
print()
print('\n'.join(details))

# Architecture Decision Records

Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [4. Defer full type-checker integration](0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md) — superseded by 0006.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.

- [7. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default](0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md) — do not feature-gate the backend crate, run it by default, or let it replace a structural entry on a clash.
- [8. Discard the parse cache whenever the build that wrote it differs](0008-parse-cache-keyed-by-build.md) — do not load cache entries without checking the payload's header against the running build.
- [9. Write each distinct prop once in the canonical output](0009-canonical-output-interns-props.md) — do not inline props in canonical JSON or derive prop ids from position.
- [10. Load dependency declarations by name, before resolution, into a shared layer](0010-load-dependency-declarations-by-name.md) — do not load dependency files by import closure, resolve against them lazily during resolution, emit their components or enums, or let them outrank a known shortcut.
- [11. Find dependency declarations through a per-package export index, not the parse cache](0011-per-package-export-index.md) — do not put dependency files in the `DtsCache` or reuse an index whose package's `package.json` changed.
- [12. Collapse large inherited dependency sources, as Storybook does](0012-collapse-large-dependency-sources.md) — do not resolve a collapsed source's props, or collapse a component's own props.

# 0013. Read React's attribute declarations in curated mode, in an index of their own

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23

## Context

When two members of an intersection declare the same prop, TypeScript intersects both types (#122). An HTML layer such as `ComponentProps<"div">` lists none of its element's attributes, yet declares them all, so a library prop named like a DOM attribute (recharts' `onTimeUpdate`) has the attribute's type as well. Only Full mode merged `@types/react`, so curated mode, which the CLI, the Vite plugin and Storybook use by default, showed the library's type alone. Merging React into the project index, as Full mode does, would also resolve every other React name in curated output (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, the handler aliases) against the real declarations and change far more than these collisions.

## Decision

In curated mode, the cold run parses `@types/react` (through the parse cache) into its own `NamedTypeIndex`, held by the revision and passed to `ResolutionContext::with_react_types`. Only the HTML-layer attribute lookup (`resolver/html.rs`, via `ResolutionContext::react_index`) reads it. It is not a fallback of the project index, so no other lookup sees React's declarations. Full mode keeps merging React into the project index; `none` mode and the dependency loader (0010) don't read React at all.

## Consequences

- A prop that collides with an attribute of the layer's element has both types in curated mode too, with both declarations listed. The attribute keeps its alias name (`ReactEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>`), because nothing else in curated mode expands React's aliases.
- One more declaration file per run: `dtsFilesParsed` rises by one in every fixture snapshot. Wall time on the five benchmark corpora is unchanged within run-to-run noise.
- On those corpora with default flags, 7 shadcn props change (`ChartContainer.children` now intersects React's `children`); nothing else does.
- Without `@types/react`, curated mode behaves as before and reports nothing, since it never required it.

## Why

Storybook's React docgen and react-docgen-typescript print a string default as its source text (`'md'`). We rewrote every string default with double quotes, which was the main remaining argTypes mismatch with React's docgen in the Storybook comparison (5 of the 7 differences).

## What

- A string-literal default keeps its source text, quotes included, like array and object literals already did. `"neutral"` and `` `Go` `` keep theirs too.
- Every output format changes, so the changeset is `minor`.
- No `.d.ts` cache bump: parameter defaults only exist in runtime source, which the cache never holds.

Stacked on #127.

## Why

#122 made a prop that two intersection members declare have both types, including an HTML layer's attribute: recharts' `onTimeUpdate` beside `ComponentProps<"div">` is the DOM handler intersected with recharts' handler. That only worked in Full mode, the one that merges `@types/react`. Curated mode, the default for the CLI, the Vite plugin and Storybook, still showed recharts' type alone.

## What

- **ADR 0013:** in curated mode the cold run parses `@types/react` (through the parse cache) into its own `NamedTypeIndex`. Only the HTML-layer attribute lookup (`resolver/html.rs`, through `ResolutionContext::react_index`) reads it; it is not a lookup fallback, so no other name resolves against React's declarations. Full mode is unchanged, and `none` mode and the dependency loader don't read React.
- The index is built once per session and carried into every watch revision.
- In curated mode the attribute keeps its alias name: `ReactEventHandler<HTMLDivElement> & ((data: unknown, index: number) => void)`.
- `docs/STATUS.md`: `--load-dependencies` becomes the default in 0.5.0 once checked against RDT on the 20 fixture libraries (agreed in review).

## Effect (five corpora with dependencies installed, before = #127)

| Corpus | Props changed | Wall time (best of 5) |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| shadcn | 7 (`ChartContainer.children` now also has React's `children`) | 72 → 69 ms |
| mantine, chakra, antd, spectrum | 0 | within noise |

Fixture snapshots change only in `dtsFilesParsed` (+1, React's declaration file).

input.content:
Updates the Entire CLI hooks for the coding agents this repo configures.

## What

- **Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`):** every Entire hook gets a timeout (30 s for session start, pre-task and prompt submit; 120 s otherwise). Adds `StopFailure`, `SubagentStart` (workflow subagents) and `SubagentStop`. The second `PostToolUse` hook now runs `post-task` on `Skill` instead of `post-todo` on `TaskCreate|TaskUpdate`. `enabledPlugins` moves to the top of the file, unchanged.
- **Removed permission:** the `deny: Read(./.entire/metadata/**)` rule is gone, so agents can read Entire's checkpoint metadata again. This is intentional; check it before merging.
- **OpenCode (`.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`):** tracks subagent (child) sessions, so a subagent's work is attributed to the top-level session and each task fires `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop` once, including nested, resumed, failed, aborted and background subagents.
- **Gemini (`.gemini/settings.json`):** Entire's hooks are removed; only `hooksConfig.enabled` remains.
- **Antigravity (`.agents/hooks.json`, new):** Entire hooks for session start, pre-tool-use, pre-invocation and stop.

No product code changes.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RDT on each installed repo (its dependencies resolvable), and caliper on the same sources with and without
# --load-dependencies. Inputs: the mirrors' component lists, mapped back to the repo paths.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT=/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp
CORPUS=$ROOT/bench-corpus
OUT=$ROOT/bench-deps
BIN=${1:-/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/release-0.2.0/target/release/caliper-docgen}
REPO=/Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/worktrees/release-0.2.0
mkdir -p "$OUT/lists" "$OUT/tsconfigs" "$OUT/results"

run() {
  local name=$1 srcdir=$2
  local src="$CORPUS/$srcdir"
  sed "s|$ROOT/bench-inputs/$name|$src|" "$ROOT/bench-inputs/lists/$name.txt" > "$OUT/lists/$name.txt"
  cat > "$OUT/tsconfigs/$name.json" <<EOF
{
  "include": ["$src/**/*.ts", "$src/**/*.tsx"],
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "noEmit": true
  }
}
EOF
  if [ ! -s "$OUT/results/$name.rdt.json" ]; then
    /usr/bin/time -l node --max-old-space-size=8192 "$ROOT/bench/rdt-dump.mjs" "$OUT/lists/$name.txt" "$OUT/tsconfigs/$name.json" \
      "$OUT/results/$name.rdt.json" 2> "$OUT/results/$name.rdt.time"
  fi
  "$BIN" extract --src "$src" --format canonical --html-attributes full --json > "$OUT/results/$name.off.json" 2>/dev/null
  "$BIN" extract --src "$src" --format canonical --html-attributes full --json --load-dependencies \
    > "$OUT/results/$name.on.json" 2>/dev/null
  echo "$name done"
}

EOF
done

input.prompt:
Investigate a performance problem in caliper-docgen (Rust, repo root is your worktree; read AGENTS.md first). Do NOT push, open PRs, or change anything outside your worktree. Read-only investigation plus local experiments; a small prototype fix in your worktree is fine if it proves the cause.

Problem: on Chakra UI's source with its dependencies installed, `--load-dependencies` makes extraction ~10x slower and ~10x heavier, even when every large inherited source is collapsed:

- Corpus: /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-corpus/chakra-ui/packages/react/src (node_modules installed in /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/bench-corpus/chakra-ui)
- Baseline binary (built from branch feat/wrapper-callee-result, equivalent for this purpose): /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp/caliper-callee
- `extract --src <corpus> --json`: 43 ms wall, 82 MiB peak RSS, stats.durationMs 51.
- `... --json --load-dependencies`: 497 ms, 1341 MiB, ~398,000 props across 600 components (each component expands Chakra's own ~705-prop SystemProperties style system).
- `... --json --load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props all`: 281 ms, 835 MiB, only 5,515 props, stats.durationMs 155.
- Measure with: `hyperfine -N -w 3 -r 15 --style basic "<cmd>"` (it reports Memory too). Bash commands touching /Users/gabe/.claude may need the sandbox disabled.

Questions:
1. With collapse=all, where do the remaining ~750 MiB and ~100 ms go? Candidates: building/holding the dependency layer (dependency_types.rs, ADR 0010/0011), resolving something per component before collapse decides (resolver/mod.rs `collapses`, ADR 0012), the per-run interface memo (resolver/memo.rs), mapped/conditional `composes` entries like `{ [K in keyof Conditions]: Nested<SystemStyleObject> }`, or output assembly/interning. Instrument with timing (std::time::Instant + eprintln behind a temporary env var) and/or macOS `/usr/bin/time -l`, or `samply` if installed. Bisect by phase.
2. Without collapse, is the 1.3 GB proportional to the 398k props (i.e., inherent to listing them), or is there avoidable duplication (e.g., props not shared via Arc as #105 intended, per-component copies of the same SystemProperties chain)?
3. Propose the smallest fix (with numbers from a prototype if feasible) that keeps output identical, or that only changes output in a justified way. Note any design decision it needs (e.g., whether project-declared large sources should collapse by default when dependencies load; ADR 0012 currently collapses dependency sources only).

Report back: a phase-by-phase breakdown with numbers, the root cause with file:line evidence, and the proposed fix with measured effect. Keep the report concise (tables and bullets).

7:**Types from other packages.** Imports resolve to any file under a source directory, `.d.ts` included, so a monorepo whose packages are all source directories resolves across them. By default, from `node_modules` only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files are read, and a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. `--load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies`) loads the declarations those names point to; it is off by default while its output is checked against RDT (ADR 0010), and becomes the default in 0.5.0 once that check passes on the 20 fixture libraries.

Stacked on #133.

## Why

With dependencies installed, react-docgen-typescript reports 363 recipe props on 126 Chakra components (`size` on 95, `variant` on 78), the main Storybook controls for Chakra users. We reported none. They come through:

```ts
interface ButtonBaseProps extends RecipeProps<"button"> {}
type RecipeProps<T> = T extends keyof ConfigRecipes ? ConfigRecipes[T]["__type"] & { recipe?: … } : { recipe?: … }
interface ConfigRecipes { button: SystemRecipeFn<ButtonVariantProps, ButtonVariantMap> }
interface SystemRecipeFn<VP, VM> { __type: Partial<VP>; … }
type ButtonVariantProps = { [K in keyof ButtonVariant]?: ConditionalValue<ButtonVariant[K]> | undefined }
```

Each step was a "cannot be used as a component's props base" warning.

## What

- **`resolver/evaluate.rs`:** evaluates what a props base needs when the operands are known, naming no library: a conditional's branch when its check is a literal and its constraint is `keyof X`, a literal or a union of literals; a member read through an indexed access (chained, through generic interface members and aliases); the keys of a mapped type's constraint (`keyof X` with X's own optionality and docs, or a literal union). Anything needing a checker (`infer`, an unbound generic) returns `None` and keeps today's warning and `composes` entry.
- **`resolve_base_as_chain`:** reduces a conditional or indexed access, and expands a mapped type into one prop per key with the key variable bound.
- **`CollectedType::Mapped`** records its key variable and `?`/`-?` modifier (the value type refers to the variable). `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 18 → 19.
- **Alias display:** an unevaluable alias's argument that the evaluator can read prints as what it reads: `ConditionalValue<"sm" | "md" | "lg" | undefined>` instead of `ConditionalValue<ButtonVariant["size"]>`, as TypeScript and RDT print it.

## Effect (before = #133)

| Corpus | Change |
| --- | --- |
| chakra | 11 components gain recipe props by default; with `--load-dependencies`, 332 of RDT's 363 recipe props (was 0) |
| antd | 224 types print an evaluated argument (`DeepClassNameType<{ root?: string; … }>`), which is how RDT prints them |
| mantine, shadcn, spectrum | none |

Speed unchanged (best of 5: chakra 64 → 56 ms, antd 72 → 75 ms). Fixture snapshots unchanged.

## Verify

- `pipeline::tests::recipe_props_evaluate_through_conditional_indexed_and_mapped_types`: exact props for the true branch (`recipe`, `size` with its description, `variant`), the false branch, and a mapped type over a literal union (both required); no warnings.
- `watch::tests::editing_a_recipe_updates_the_props_its_mapped_type_lists`: editing only the recipes file adds `shape` to `Button` and matches a cold `extract()`.
- Two existing tests used `'x' extends string ? …` as their unresolvable conditional; it now evaluates, so they use an `infer` instead and assert the exact `composes` text.
- `cargo nextest run --workspace` (776 pass), `just lint doc-check typos`.

## Evaluating a props base with known operands (`resolver/evaluate.rs`)

`resolve_base_as_chain` evaluates three kinds of props base when their operands are known, without a checker: a conditional whose check is a literal and whose constraint is `keyof X`, a literal or a union of literals (`RecipeProps<"button">` picks its branch); an indexed access, chained and through generic interface members and aliases (`ConfigRecipes["button"]["__type"]`); and a mapped type over `keyof X` or a literal union, one prop per key with the key variable bound. A homomorphic mapped type without `?`/`-?` keeps each source member's optionality and description. Anything else (an `infer`, an unbound generic) evaluates to `None` and keeps the warning and `composes` entry. `alias_display` uses the same evaluator for an argument that reads a member (`ConditionalValue<ButtonVariant["size"]>` prints the member's type). Lookups record their files, so editing the declarations re-resolves dependents.

content.text:
Mostly yes: the new rules are generic TypeScript semantics, not library rules. But two of my changes took shortcuts shaped by Mantine and Chakra, and the older code still has about a dozen library-specific shortcuts.

**Generic, no change needed:**

| Change | Why it's generic |
|---|---|
| #127 string defaults keep source quotes | Source text, no cases |
| #128 curated mode reads React's attributes | React is the platform. It isn't a library-specific case. |
| #134 evaluator for conditional, indexed and mapped types | A subset of TypeScript's semantics; anything outside the subset falls back as before |
| Watch ignores file-read events, test race fixes, harness repair | Bugs, not rules |

**Where I narrowed to the case in front of me:**

1. **#129 only adds the inline-object members of the factory's result type.** TypeScript's rule is simply "the component's props are its type's props parameter". I narrowed it because `Payload['props']` used to be unevaluable and would have warned. #134 can now evaluate that, so the general version is possible: when the callee's result type is known, use it as the props source. That would retire the guesswork in `wrapper.rs` for those callees: the `props` payload member, the `*Props` name suffix, and the element-name list.
2. **The `export *` fix only finds generic functions.** I recorded what the Mantine case needed. A barrel re-exporting a non-generic function, a const or a component through `export *` still isn't followed. The general fix is to record every exported value declaration.
3. **All tuning was measured on the same five libraries against react-docgen-typescript.** Nothing checks for overfitting. A held-out set of libraries that were never used for tuning would catch it.

**Existing special-case debt (task #7):**
- **`known.rs`:** 16 named shortcuts, several of them library names. Examples: `HTMLChakraProps`, `MantineColor`, `ThemingProps`, `StylesApiProps`, `SxProps`, `OverridableStringUnion`. They exist because the resolver couldn't evaluate those libraries' conditional or mapped types. The evaluator and dependency loading may make some unnecessary.
- **`primitives.rs`:** a hand table of `CSSProperties`/`HTMLAttributes` member types. With React's declarations now indexed, these could be looked up instead.
- **`wrapper.rs`:** the heuristics listed in point 1, plus a comment naming Mantine's `_Box` spelling.
- **`react_types.rs`:** 66 React and DOM names. These are platform names, and the curated attribute list is a deliberate product choice, so I'd keep them.

**Proposed plan,** keeping the goal in view (Storybook docs that match what Storybook users see, at caliper's speed):
1. Generalize #129 so the callee's result type is the props source, keeping the heuristics only as a fallback when the callee is unknown.
2. Record all exported values for barrel resolution.
3. Run task #7 as a measured experiment. Disable each `known.rs` shortcut in turn, compare against react-docgen-typescript with and without dependencies, and delete every shortcut the generic resolver now matches.
4. Add 3–4 held-out libraries to the scorecard, reported on every PR, so no rule gets tuned to the benchmark set.

Say go to run all four, or pick which ones.

result: The recent PRs (#127–#134) are generic TypeScript rules apart from two shortcuts in #129 and the `export *` fix. The real special-case debt is 16 named shortcuts in `known.rs` plus the `wrapper.rs` heuristics, with a four-step plan to generalize them and add a held-out benchmark.
Let's address these shorcuts please

I'll work through it in four steps, each measured against react-docgen-typescript:

1. **Barrels:** count any exported declaration (from the export list each file already records), not just generic functions.
2. **Wrapper props:** when a factory's result type is known, use its props parameter as the component's props. The `props`-member and `*Props`-suffix guesses become a fallback for unknown factories.
3. **`known.rs` shortcuts:** these only fire in code that uses a library (an app importing Chakra, MUI, Mantine or cva), and none of the five benchmark repos is such an app. So I'll build small consumer apps with those packages installed. They also serve as the held-out set. Then I'll measure each shortcut off versus on and remove the ones the generic resolver now handles.
4. **`primitives.rs`'s `CSSProperties` table:** replace it with lookups in React's own declarations.

The extractor records every generic function's result in `SourceData::function_results`: the return annotation, or the type its only top-level `return … as T` asserts. `callee::result_props` binds the callee's type parameters to the call's type arguments, follows aliases to the first React component type (`NamedExoticComponent

`, `FC

`, a call signature, …) and adds P's inline object members (`{ component?: any; renderRoot?: … }`) that the component doesn't already have. Other members of P (`Payload['props']`, `RefAttributes<…>`) are left to the selection, so this never warns. The callee's file is a recorded dependency, so editing the factory re-resolves the components it builds; `follow_reexports` treats a recorded function as a declaration, so `export *` barrels reach it.

# 0014. A loaded declaration wins over a known shortcut; shortcuts are fallbacks

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23

## Context

`known.rs` resolves library types by name (`HTMLChakraProps`, `SxProps`, cva's `VariantProps`, …) because the structural resolver couldn't expand their declarations. ADR 0010 kept that order for loaded dependencies: a project declaration, then a shortcut, then the dependency's own declaration. Measured against react-docgen-typescript on a consumer app with Chakra, MUI, Mantine, cva and react-aria-components installed, the loaded declarations now beat the shortcuts: Chakra's `HTMLChakraProps` gives 139 of RDT's props instead of 1, its `ButtonProps` 146 instead of 0, and Mantine's `StylesApiProps` 8 instead of 3. Only cva's `VariantProps`, which needs inference (`Parameters<C>[0]`), still needs its shortcut.

## Decision

- **Order:** a declaration, the project's or a loaded dependency's, then a known shortcut, then a React builtin (`resolver/precedence.rs`).
- **Fallback:** at the props-chain level, a declaration that evaluates to nothing (no props, no inherited layer, something left unevaluated) gives way to a shortcut of the same name, if one exists (`chain::known_fallback`). Its diagnostics are dropped with it.
- **Shortcuts kept:** only where the fallback measurably beats an unresolved name: the variant-props family, react-aria's `RenderProps`/`SlotProps`, and `HTMLChakraProps`/`HTMLArkProps`/`HTMLStyledProps` (an HTML layer when the package isn't loaded), plus React's own `PropsWithChildren`, `ComponentProps` and the like.
- **Shortcuts removed:** `SxProps`/`SystemStyleObject`/`SystemCssProperties` (printed worse text than the name itself), `OverridableStringUnion`, `ThemingProps`, `StylesApiProps` (opaque placeholders a loaded declaration beats), and the no-op `MantineColor`/`MantineSize`/`MantineRadius` arm.

## Consequences

- With `--load-dependencies`, a consumer of a component library gets the library's real props. Without it, a removed shortcut's name stays an unresolved named reference with the usual warning, as any other uninstalled package's type does; `PropType::SxProps` is no longer produced.
- A new shortcut needs the same evidence: it must beat the declaration, or stand in where the declaration can't be read, on code that uses the library.
- Library repos are unaffected: their own declarations already won (no change on the five benchmark corpora).

Stacked on #134.

## Why

An audit of the recent work for special cases versus generic rules found three places where the code was shaped by the libraries we tuned on rather than by TypeScript's rules: library-name shortcuts in `known.rs` that outranked even a loaded declaration (ADR 0010), the wrapper-props rule from #129 taking only inline object members, and `export *` resolution that only found types plus the generic functions #129 needed.

## What

- **Declarations before shortcuts (ADR 0014):** a declaration, the project's or a loaded dependency's, now wins over a known shortcut. A shortcut is the fallback when the package isn't loaded, or, at the props-chain level, when its declaration evaluates to nothing (cva's `VariantProps` needs `Parameters<C>[0]`).
- **Shortcuts removed,** each measured against react-docgen-typescript on a consumer app (Chakra 3, MUI 6, Mantine 7, cva, react-aria-components installed, never used for tuning): `SxProps`/`SystemStyleObject`/`SystemCssProperties` (printed worse text than the name), `OverridableStringUnion`, `ThemingProps`, `StylesApiProps` (placeholders the declaration beats) and the no-op `MantineColor`/`MantineSize`/`MantineRadius` arm. Kept as fallbacks: the variant-props family, `RenderProps`/`SlotProps`, `HTMLChakraProps`/`HTMLArkProps`/`HTMLStyledProps`, and React's own.
- **Wrapper props from the callee's result:** a generic factory's result type is now the component's props source when it resolves (`Payload['props'] & … & { component?: any; … }`), not just its inline members; the extractor's payload and `*Props` guesses are the fallback. `any` absorbs an intersection, as in TypeScript.
- **Barrels:** an `export *` hop counts any declaration the file exports (from its own export list), renamed exports included.

## Effect

Consumer app, against RDT (props RDT reports that caliper has / with the same type text):

| Component | Before, deps loaded | After, deps loaded | Before, no deps | After, no deps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Panel` (`HTMLChakraProps<"div">`) | 1 / 1 | 139 / 138 | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| `SubmitButton` (Chakra `ButtonProps`) | 0 / 0 | 146 / 142 | 0 | 0 |

| `Card` (MUI `SxProps`) | 2 / 1 | 2 / 2 | 2 / 1 | 2 / 2 |
| `Badge` (cva `VariantProps`) | 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 |

Not changed: `primitives.rs`'s `CSSProperties[key]` table. RDT prints csstype's alias names (`Padding<string | number>`), which live in `csstype`, a package React's declarations import and we don't load; replacing the table needs that loading and an alias-printing decision.

Stacked on #135.

## Why

`--load-dependencies` cost Chakra's repo 0.5 s and 1.3 GB (43 ms and 82 MiB without), which blocks making it the default. Collapsing every large source still left 835 MiB, so the cost wasn't the listed props. Profiling found three generic causes, none Chakra-specific:

- **`keyof` walks resolved every member's type to read only names.** Chakra's `Assign<T, U> = Omit<T, keyof U> & U` makes each component compute `keyof` over its ~705-prop style system; each walk resolved all member types and produced ~1,300 diagnostics (`resolver/alias.rs`, the `KeyOf` arm of `resolve_key_set`).
- **Memo replays cloned those diagnostics into every component** (~750k copies, 216 MB of strings), and assembly then hashed every copy.
- **Memo recordings weren't keyed by mode,** so a `keyof`-mode recording could fill the slots normal resolution needed.

## What

- **`ResolveState::keys_only`:** set for a `keyof` operand; member types, inline object fields, HTML-layer merges and mapped-type values are not resolved, only names. Recordings made in it answer only states in it.
- **Shared diagnostic chunks:** memo recordings hold `Arc<[Diagnostic]>`; a replay pushes a pointer, and `DiagnosticSet::extend_shared` hashes each chunk once.
- **Memo keys include the mode** (`expand_all`, `keys_only`), and an identical recording isn't stored twice.

## Effect

| Chakra repo | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--load-dependencies` | 567 ms, 1.4 GiB | 255 ms, 0.3 GiB |
| default | 38 ms, 0.1 GiB | 39 ms, 0.1 GiB |

Props, types and defaults are identical on all five corpora; fixture snapshots unchanged. Diagnostics about member types of `keyof` operands, which the component never lists, are no longer produced.

Not fixed: at cold start ~15 workers still resolve the same large interface concurrently; making them wait risks deadlocking rayon on cyclic types. The profiling also found the memo can replay a recording that differs from a fresh resolution (Chakra's `CodeBlockCollapseIndicator.children` parent); this change happens to match the fresh result, and it deserves its own test.

## Verify

- `cargo nextest run --workspace` (769 pass), `just lint`; output compared prop by prop and type by type against #135 on the five corpora.

docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md:68:RDT natively supports a `composes: string[]` field on each component — "these props come from this named type, listed by reference, not flattened into `props`." This tool's resolver reuses that exact mechanism for a second, distinct purpose: recording every type it gave up trying to resolve. `ResolvedChain::give_up` (`crates/core/src/resolver/mod.rs:380-386`) is "the sanctioned 'give up' entry point for every 'this type couldn't be followed further, stop here' path" — it pushes an optional `Diagnostic` and then calls `empty_with_compose(type_name)`, which sets `composes: vec![type_name]`. Every unresolvable type (a conditional type, a generic pattern the resolver doesn't understand, a cycle) lands in `composes` instead of silently vanishing from `props`.
docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md:149:- **Nesting/placement correctness.** Because the check is `schema_str.contains(field_name)` over the _entire flattened schema string_, a field name appearing anywhere in the schema — even under a completely unrelated object — satisfies the check. A field accidentally documented under the wrong parent object would still pass.
docs/architecture/cli-commands.md:69:The `composes` field (react-docgen's own "props come from this type, listed by name instead of flattened" fallback for unresolvable types) was populated by the resolver but **used to be silently dropped by `serialize_rdt`** — the `rdt_output_includes_composes` test (`extract.rs:202-227`) and its comment block point at the resolver-side fix in `pipeline::tests::test_unresolvable_intersection_member_records_raw_type_in_composes` as the other half of that bug. If a new `ComponentEntry` field is ever added on the core side, check `pipeline::rdt` by hand — nothing enforces that every core field round-trips into this hand-written serializer, which is exactly the class of bug `composes` fell into.
docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md:59:**Invariant 1 — an interface name resolves differently depending on which level asked.** At the type level (`resolve_named`, called for a _field's_ type — e.g. `value: SomeInterface`), a matched interface returns `PropType::Named { name, args }` — bare, unexpanded. At the chain level (`resolve_props_chain`, called for a _props-base_ type — the component's own props type, or an `extends` target), the same interface expands via `resolve_interface_chain` into real `ParsedProp`s. This split exists because a field whose type happens to be an interface should show as a named type reference in RDT-compatible output, not get flattened into an anonymous object — but a component's _own_ props type (or something it extends) must actually contribute fields. Conflating the two would either over-expand nested interface-typed fields into inline objects, or under-expand a component's own extends chain.
docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md:113:- `generic_alias_with_structured_args` — used when the caller already has a _structured_ `CollectedType` argument (e.g. `SelectRootBaseProps<T>` passed as another generic alias's own argument) — skips the string round-trip entirely, so nested generics and `keyof` operands survive substitution intact. `resolve_base_as_chain` (alias.rs) prefers this path when available, falling back to the string-based path only when arguments are already flattened to display strings.
docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md:121:Mirroring the `OpaqueDetail` split at the chain level: `ResolvedChain::empty()` is the base accumulator every real resolution path builds up from (interface chain resolution, extends merging). `ResolvedChain::empty_with_compose(type_name)` and `ResolvedChain::give_up(type_name, diag, state)` are the two sanctioned "this type contributes nothing further" signals — `give_up` additionally pushes a diagnostic first. **Invariant 6:** every give-up path in `chain.rs`/`alias.rs` must go through one of these two, never a bare `ResolvedChain::default()` — a bare `default()` was itself a fixed bug (`test_self_referential_extends_emits_diagnostic_instead_of_silent_default`, `test_literal_union_as_props_base_emits_diagnostic_instead_of_silent_default`): the cycle-detected branch and the literal-union-as-props-base branch both used to return a silent empty chain with no trace. `composes` — react-docgen's own field for "props come from this type, named instead of flattened" — is populated by every give-up path today specifically so a degraded resolution still surfaces _something_ in RDT-compatible output rather than silently vanishing to zero props.

Stacked on #136.

## Why

A union built from aliases that resolve to the same type listed that type once per alias. React Spectrum's `CollectionChildren<T>` printed `ReactNode | null | ReactNode | null | (ReactNode | null | ReactNode | null)[] | …` on 21 components; Chakra's `For.each` (`T[] | readonly T[]`) printed `T[] | T[]`; react-hook-form's signatures repeated `FieldPath<T>[]`. TypeScript lists each member once.

## What

- `resolver::primitives::union_of` forms every resolved union: a member that is a union contributes its members, a member equal to an earlier one is dropped, a single member stands alone.
- Used by inline unions, alias unions (which didn't flatten before), union-of-props merges and function signatures.

## Effect

| Corpus | Props with a repeated union member, before → after (with deps) | Printed type text changed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spectrum | 21 → 0 | 21 (`children`, shown above) |
| chakra | 1 → 0 | 1 (`For.each` → `T[]`) |
| shadcn | 1 → 0 | 0 |
| mantine, antd | 0 → 0 | 0 |

About 3,900 more props change only in `--json` structure: an alias's union members now sit in the outer union instead of a nested `{"kind":"union"}`. Their text is unchanged. Timing unchanged; fixture snapshots unchanged.

Not fixed: `readonly T[]` still prints as `T[]`, since `PropType::Array` has no readonly flag.

## Verify

- `cargo nextest run --workspace` (770 pass), `just lint doc-check typos`.
- `pipeline::tests::a_union_lists_each_member_once_however_it_was_spelled` asserts the exact types for alias, nested-literal, readonly-array and signature cases.

print()

Stacked on #137.

## Why

A component declared inside a function body exists per call: a factory's returned component (`const Result = forwardRef(…); return Result;`) or a story's local helper. No module imports it by that name, and RDT never reports one. Caliper documented them: React Spectrum listed two `Result` components from `createLeafComponent`/`createBranchComponent`, and antd's local `PurePanel` (0 props) took the key of the module-level `PurePanel`.

## What

- `SourceDataCollector::function_depth`, counted in `visit_function_body` (functions, methods and arrows alike).
- Inside a body, a declaration a detector would map gets an Info `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` ("declared inside a function body, so no module can import it") instead of a mapping. A local no detector maps produces nothing; before, each PascalCase local (`const Comp = asChild ? Slot : "button"`) was reported as a failed candidate.

## Effect

| Corpus | Components removed | None of them in RDT's output | Skip diagnostics, before → after |
| --- | --: | --- | --- |
| mantine | 2 (`Component`, `Extended`) | yes | 60 → 52 |
| chakra | 2 (`Comp`, `OverlayViewportItem`) | yes | 152 → 143 |
| shadcn | 0 | | 300 → 263 |
| antd | 5 (`Adapter`, `Calendar`, `Picker`, local `PurePanel`, `RangePicker`) | yes | 164 → 149 |
| spectrum | 3 (`Result` ×2, `Wrapper`) | yes | 731 → 609 |

antd's module-level `PurePanel` now has its own key and its props. The shadcn fixture snapshot drops one such skip diagnostic. `.d.ts` files have no bodies, so the parse cache needs no schema bump.

- `cargo nextest run --workspace` (771 pass), `just lint doc-check typos`.
- `extractor::tests::a_component_declared_inside_a_function_body_is_reported_not_mapped` covers a local `forwardRef` binding, function declaration, class and annotated arrow, with the exact mappings and messages.

import json, os, subprocess, sys

deps = ['--load-dependencies'] if '--deps' in sys.argv else []

    ('spectrum', f'{B}/bench-corpus/react-spectrum/packages'),
    ('consumers', f'{B}/consumers/src'),
]


def run(src, env_extra):
    env = dict(os.environ, **env_extra)
    out = json.loads(subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json'] + deps, capture_output=True, check=True, env=env).stdout)
    props = out.get('props', {})
    flat = {}
    for key, c in out['components'].items():
        for name, p in c['props'].items():
            p = props.get(p, p) if isinstance(p, str) else p
            flat[(key, name)] = json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True)
    return flat

    for k in diff[:SHOW]:
        print('  ', k)

Stacked on #138.

## Why

#136's profiling found the interface-chain memo replaying a recording that differed from a fresh resolution (Chakra's `CodeBlockCollapseIndicator.children` parent). #136 put the resolution mode in the memo key, which happened to fix it, but no test covered the mode bits.

## What

Two cases for the existing reused-vs-fresh harness (`resolve_shared`, now `resolve_shared_with` to take options), each with both components reaching the shared interface at the same depth so only the mode separates the recordings:

- `keys_only`: a `keyof Base` walk records `Base` with `unknown` member types; a component inheriting `Base` must get its real types.
- `expand_all`: `Pick<Big, "p0">` records `Big` expanded; a component inheriting `Big` under `--collapse-inherited-props all` must get a collapsed layer.

Each test fails when its mode bit is removed from the key and from `Recording::applies_to`.

## Memo-on vs memo-off on the corpora

With a temporary switch that bypasses the memo (not committed), output was identical prop by prop on all six corpora, with and without `--load-dependencies` (Chakra with deps: 470,946 props), and identical across repeated multi-threaded runs.

## Verify

CustomSpacing : …`. It now prints the alias name with its arguments as written, the way TypeScript does. Aliases to literal unions and objects still expand, so enum controls are unchanged.

- **An alias over an indexed access that can't be evaluated keeps its name:** with `--load-dependencies`, `z.infer<typeof schema>` printed as `typeof schema["_output"]`. Like an alias over a conditional or mapped type, it now shows as `z.infer<typeof schema>`, and project aliases such as `type Side = (typeof SIDE_OPTIONS)[number]` show as `Side` instead of their source. An indexed access on a declared type passed as an argument (`z.infer<Parsed>`) now evaluates.
- **`typeof X` keeps its `typeof`:** a value's type that can't be evaluated printed as the bare value name (`ReturnType<useTree>`, `JSON.parse`); it now prints as `ReturnType<typeof useTree>` and `typeof JSON.parse`, as TypeScript does.

src, component, prop, needle, *bins = sys.argv[1:]

    out = json.loads(subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--format', 'rdt'], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout)
    docs = out if isinstance(out, list) else list(out.values())
    for doc in docs:
        if doc['displayName'] == component and prop in doc['props']:
            t = doc['props'][prop]['type']
            text = t.get('raw') or t.get('name')
            print(binary.rsplit('/', 1)[-1], text.count(needle), len(text))
            break

"""Per corpus, over props both binaries and RDT (with deps) report: how many have RDT's exact type name, and RDT's kind
(enum vs not), for each binary, plus timing. Usage: rdt_agree.py BEFORE AFTER [--deps] [--show N]"""
import json, subprocess, sys, time

B = '/Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/ba6a68d6/tmp'
before, after = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
deps = ['--load-dependencies'] if '--deps' in sys.argv else []
SHOW = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--show') + 1]) if '--show' in sys.argv else 0
CORPORA = [
    ('mantine', f'{B}/bench-corpus/mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src'),
    ('chakra', f'{B}/bench-corpus/chakra-ui/packages/react/src'),
    ('shadcn', f'{B}/bench-corpus/shadcn-ui/apps/v4'),
    ('antd', f'{B}/bench-corpus/ant-design/components'),
    ('spectrum', f'{B}/bench-corpus/react-spectrum/packages'),
]


def norm(t):
    return ' '.join((t or '').split())


def caliper(binary, src):
    start = time.time()
    out = json.loads(subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--format', 'rdt', '--html-attributes', 'full'] + deps, capture_output=True, check=True).stdout)
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    docs = out if isinstance(out, list) else list(out.values())
    return {(d['filePath'], d['displayName'], n): norm(p['type'].get('name')) for d in docs for n, p in d['props'].items()}, elapsed


print('| Corpus | Shared props | Type name = RDT, before → after | Enum agrees, before → after | s before → after |')
print('| --- | --: | --- | --- | --- |')
examples = []
for name, src in CORPORA:
    rdt = {}
    for d in json.load(open(f'{B}/bench-deps/results/{name}.rdt-dump.json')):
        for n, p in d['props'].items():
            t = p.get('type')
            rdt[(d['file'], d['name'], n)] = norm(t if isinstance(t, str) else json.dumps(t))
    a, ta = caliper(before, src)
    b, tb = caliper(after, src)
    keys = rdt.keys() & a.keys() & b.keys()
    same_a = sum(a[k] == rdt[k] for k in keys)
    same_b = sum(b[k] == rdt[k] for k in keys)
    enum_a = sum((a[k] == 'enum') == (rdt[k] == 'enum') for k in keys)
    enum_b = sum((b[k] == 'enum') == (rdt[k] == 'enum') for k in keys)
    print(f'| {name} | {len(keys):,} | {same_a:,} → {same_b:,} | {enum_a:,} → {enum_b:,} | {ta:.2f} → {tb:.2f} |')
    worse = [k for k in sorted(keys) if a[k] == rdt[k] and b[k] != rdt[k]]
    better = [k for k in sorted(keys) if a[k] != rdt[k] and b[k] == rdt[k]]
    examples.append((name, len(worse), len(better), [(k[1], k[2], rdt[k][:60], b[k][:80]) for k in worse[:SHOW]]))
print()
for name, worse, better, ex in examples:
    print(f'{name}: {better} now match RDT, {worse} no longer match')
    for e in ex:
        print('   ', e)

"""Best-of-N wall ms on one corpus for one binary with and without an env var, interleaved. Usage: envtime.py BIN SRC VAR [N] [--deps]"""
import os, subprocess, sys, time

binary, src, var = sys.argv[1:4]
n = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 and sys.argv[4].isdigit() else 15
deps = ['--load-dependencies'] if '--deps' in sys.argv else []
best = {'off': 1e9, 'on': 1e9}
for _ in range(n):
    for label, env in (('off', dict(os.environ)), ('on', dict(os.environ, **{var: '1'}))):
        start = time.time()
        subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json'] + deps, capture_output=True, check=True, env=env)
        best[label] = min(best[label], time.time() - start)
print({k: round(v * 1000, 1) for k, v in best.items()}, f'(on = {var} set)')

1	# 0014. A loaded declaration wins over a known shortcut; shortcuts are fallbacks
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	`known.rs` resolves library types by name (`HTMLChakraProps`, `SxProps`, cva's `VariantProps`, …) because the structural resolver couldn't expand their declarations. ADR 0010 kept that order for loaded dependencies: a project declaration, then a shortcut, then the dependency's own declaration. Measured against react-docgen-typescript on a consumer app with Chakra, MUI, Mantine, cva and react-aria-components installed, the loaded declarations now beat the shortcuts: Chakra's `HTMLChakraProps` gives 139 of RDT's props instead of 1, its `ButtonProps` 146 instead of 0, and Mantine's `StylesApiProps` 8 instead of 3. Only cva's `VariantProps`, which needs inference (`Parameters<C>[0]`), still needs its shortcut.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	- **Order:** a declaration, the project's or a loaded dependency's, then a known shortcut, then a React builtin (`resolver/precedence.rs`).
12	- **Fallback:** at the props-chain level, a declaration that evaluates to nothing (no props, no inherited layer, something left unevaluated) gives way to a shortcut of the same name, if one exists (`chain::known_fallback`). Its diagnostics are dropped with it.
13	- **Shortcuts kept:** only where the fallback measurably beats an unresolved name: the variant-props family, react-aria's `RenderProps`/`SlotProps`, and `HTMLChakraProps`/`HTMLArkProps`/`HTMLStyledProps` (an HTML layer when the package isn't loaded), plus React's own `PropsWithChildren`, `ComponentProps` and the like.
14	- **Shortcuts removed:** `SxProps`/`SystemStyleObject`/`SystemCssProperties` (printed worse text than the name itself), `OverridableStringUnion`, `ThemingProps`, `StylesApiProps` (opaque placeholders a loaded declaration beats), and the no-op `MantineColor`/`MantineSize`/`MantineRadius` arm.
15	
16	## Consequences
17	
18	- With `--load-dependencies`, a consumer of a component library gets the library's real props. Without it, a removed shortcut's name stays an unresolved named reference with the usual warning, as any other uninstalled package's type does; `PropType::SxProps` is no longer produced.
19	- A new shortcut needs the same evidence: it must beat the declaration, or stand in where the declaration can't be read, on code that uses the library.
20	- Library repos are unaffected: their own declarations already won (no change on the five benchmark corpora).
21

1	# 0013. Read React's attribute declarations in curated mode, in an index of their own
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-23
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	When two members of an intersection declare the same prop, TypeScript intersects both types (#122). An HTML layer such as `ComponentProps<"div">` lists none of its element's attributes, yet declares them all, so a library prop named like a DOM attribute (recharts' `onTimeUpdate`) has the attribute's type as well. Only Full mode merged `@types/react`, so curated mode, which the CLI, the Vite plugin and Storybook use by default, showed the library's type alone. Merging React into the project index, as Full mode does, would also resolve every other React name in curated output (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, the handler aliases) against the real declarations and change far more than these collisions.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	In curated mode, the cold run parses `@types/react` (through the parse cache) into its own `NamedTypeIndex`, held by the revision and passed to `ResolutionContext::with_react_types`. Only the HTML-layer attribute lookup (`resolver/html.rs`, via `ResolutionContext::react_index`) reads it. It is not a fallback of the project index, so no other lookup sees React's declarations. Full mode keeps merging React into the project index; `none` mode and the dependency loader (0010) don't read React at all.
12	
13	## Consequences
14	
15	- A prop that collides with an attribute of the layer's element has both types in curated mode too, with both declarations listed. The attribute keeps its alias name (`ReactEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>`), because nothing else in curated mode expands React's aliases.
16	- One more declaration file per run: `dtsFilesParsed` rises by one in every fixture snapshot. Wall time on the five benchmark corpora is unchanged within run-to-run noise.
17	- On those corpora with default flags, 7 shadcn props change (`ChartContainer.children` now intersects React's `children`); nothing else does.
18	- Without `@types/react`, curated mode behaves as before and reports nothing, since it never required it.
19
